{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T13:59:15.081Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_IQD86PqWTN1BHH2U11SLlOig","output":"Chunk ID: 6e0238\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1905\nOutput:\nimport logging\nimport time\nfrom typing import Dict, List, Optional, Protocol, Tuple\n\nimport numpy.random as rnd\n\nfrom alns.Outcome import Outcome\nfrom alns.Result import Result\nfrom alns.State import State\nfrom alns.Statistics import Statistics\nfrom alns.accept import AcceptanceCriterion\nfrom alns.select import OperatorSelectionScheme\nfrom alns.stop import StoppingCriterion\n\n\nclass _OperatorType(Protocol):\n    __name__: str\n\n    def __call__(\n        self,\n        state: State,\n        rng: rnd.Generator,\n        **kwargs,\n    ) -> State:\n        ...  # pragma: no cover\n\n\nclass _CallbackType(Protocol):\n    __name__: str\n\n    def __call__(self, state: State, rng: rnd.Generator, **kwargs):\n        ...  # pragma: no cover\n\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass ALNS:\n    \"\"\"\n    Implements the adaptive large neighbourhood search (ALNS) algorithm.\n    The implementation optimises for a minimisation problem, as explained\n    in the text by Pisinger and Røpke (2010).\n\n    .. note::\n\n        Like the operators passed into the ALNS instance, any registered\n        callback functions (registered via :meth:`~alns.ALNS.ALNS.on_best`,\n        :meth:`~alns.ALNS.ALNS.on_better`, :meth:`~alns.ALNS.ALNS.on_accept`,\n        or :meth:`~alns.ALNS.ALNS.on_reject`) should take a candidate\n        :class:`~alns.State.State` and :class:`~numpy.random.Generator` as\n        arguments. Unlike the operators, no solution should be returned: if\n        desired, the given candidate solution should be modified in-place\n        instead. Note that this solution is **not** evaluated again (so a\n        rejected candidate solution will stay rejected!).\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    rng\n        Optional random number generator (RNG). When passed, this generator\n        is used for operator selection and general computations requiring\n        random numbers. It is also passed to the destroy and repair operators,\n        as a second argument.\n\n    References\n    ----------\n    .. [1] Pisinger, D., and Røpke, S. (2010). Large Neighborhood Search. In\n           M. Gendreau (Ed.), *Handbook of Metaheuristics* (2 ed., pp. 399\n           - 420). Springer.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, rng: rnd.Generator = rnd.default_rng()):\n        self._rng = rng\n\n        self._d_ops: Dict[str, _OperatorType] = {}\n        self._r_ops: Dict[str, _OperatorType] = {}\n\n        # Registers callback for each possible evaluation outcome.\n        self._on_outcome: Dict[Outcome, _CallbackType] = {}\n\n    @property\n    def destroy_operators(self) -> List[Tuple[str, _OperatorType]]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Returns the destroy operators set for the ALNS algorithm.\n\n        Returns\n        -------\n        list\n            A list of (name, operator) tuples. Their order is the same as the\n            one in which they were passed to the ALNS instance.\n        \"\"\"\n        return list(self._d_ops.items())\n\n    @property\n    def repair_operators(self) -> List[Tuple[str, _OperatorType]]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Returns the repair operators set for the ALNS algorithm.\n\n        Returns\n        -------\n        list\n            A list of (name, operator) tuples. Their order is the same as the\n            one in which they were passed to the ALNS instance.\n        \"\"\"\n        return list(self._r_ops.items())\n\n    def add_destroy_operator(\n        self, op: _OperatorType, name: Optional[str] = None\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Adds a destroy operator to the heuristic instance.\n\n        .. warning::\n\n            A destroy operator will receive the current solution state\n            maintained by the ALNS instance, not a copy. Make sure to modify\n            a **copy** of this state in the destroy operator, created using,\n            for example, :func:`copy.copy` or :func:`copy.deepcopy`.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        op\n            An operator that, when applied to the current state, returns a new\n            state reflecting its implemented destroy action. Its second\n            argument is the RNG passed to the ALNS instance.\n        name\n            Optional name argument, naming the operator. When not passed, the\n            function name is used instead.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.debug(f\"Adding destroy operator {op.__name__}.\")\n        self._d_ops[op.__name__ if name is None else name] = op\n\n    def add_repair_operator(\n        self, op: _OperatorType, name: Optional[str] = None\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Adds a repair operator to the heuristic instance.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        op\n            An operator that, when applied to the destroyed state, returns a\n            new state reflecting its implemented repair action. Its second\n            argument is the RNG passed to the ALNS instance.\n        name\n            Optional name argument, naming the operator. When not passed, the\n            function name is used instead.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.debug(f\"Adding repair operator {op.__name__}.\")\n        self._r_ops[name if name else op.__name__] = op\n\n    def iterate(\n        self,\n        initial_solution: State,\n        op_select: OperatorSelectionScheme,\n        accept: AcceptanceCriterion,\n        stop: StoppingCriterion,\n        **kwargs,\n    ) -> Result:\n        \"\"\"\n        Runs the adaptive large neighbourhood search heuristic [1], using the\n        previously set destroy and repair operators. The first solution is set\n        to the passed-in initial solution, and then subsequent solutions are\n        computed by iteratively applying the operators.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        initial_solution\n            The initial solution, as a State object.\n        op_select\n            The operator selection scheme to use for selecting operators.\n            See also the ``alns.select`` module for an overview.\n        accept\n            The acceptance criterion to use for candidate states.\n            See also the ``alns.accept`` module for an overview.\n        stop\n            The stopping criterion to use for stopping the iterations.\n            See also the ``alns.stop`` module for an overview.\n        **kwargs\n            Optional keyword arguments. These are passed to the operators and\n            any registered callbacks.\n\n        Raises\n        ------\n        ValueError\n            When the parameters do not meet requirements.\n\n        Returns\n        -------\n        Result\n            A result object, containing the best solution and some additional\n            statistics.\n\n        References\n        ----------\n        .. [1] Pisinger, D., & Røpke, S. (2010). Large Neighborhood Search. In\n               M. Gendreau (Ed.), *Handbook of Metaheuristics* (2 ed., pp. 399\n               - 420). Springer.\n\n        .. [2] S. Røpke and D. Pisinger (2006). A unified heuristic for a large\n               class of vehicle routing problems with backhauls. *European\n               Journal of Operational Research*, 171: 750-775.\n        \"\"\"\n        if len(self.destroy_operators) == 0 or len(self.repair_operators) == 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"Missing destroy or repair operators.\")\n\n        curr = best = initial_solution\n        init_obj = initial_solution.objective()\n\n        logger.debug(f\"Initial solution has objective {init_obj:.2f}.\")\n\n        stats = Statistics()\n        stats.collect_objective(init_obj)\n        stats.collect_runtime(time.perf_counter())\n\n        while not stop(self._rng, best, curr):\n            d_idx, r_idx = op_select(self._rng, best, curr)\n\n            d_name, d_operator = self.destroy_operators[d_idx]\n            r_name, r_operator = self.repair_operators[r_idx]\n\n"}}

Initially, :math:`T` is set to\n    :math:`T_\\\\text{start}`.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    start_threshold\n        The initial threshold :math:`T_\\\\text{start} \\\\ge 0`.\n    end_threshold\n        The final threshold :math:`T_\\\\text{end} \\\\ge 0`.\n    step\n        The updating step size :math:`\\\\gamma \\\\ge 0`.\n    method\n        The updating method, one of {'linear', 'exponential'}. By default, `cmp_best` is True, in which\n        case RRT checks whether the difference between the candidate and best\n        solution is below the threshold [2]. If `cmp_best` is False, RRT takes\n        the difference between the candidate and current solution instead. This\n        yields the behaviour of threshold accepting (TA), see [3] for details.\n\n    References\n    ----------\n    .. [1] Santini, A., Ropke, S. & Hvattum, L.M. A comparison of acceptance\n           criteria for the adaptive large neighbourhood search metaheuristic.\n           *Journal of Heuristics* (2018) 24 (5): 783-815.\n    .. [2] Dueck, G. New optimization heuristics: The great deluge algorithm\n           and the record-to-record travel. *Journal of Computational Physics*\n           (1993) 104 (1): 86-92.\n    .. [3] Dueck, G., Scheuer, T. Threshold accepting: A general purpose\n         optimization algorithm appearing superior to simulated annealing.\n         *Journal of Computational Physics* (1990) 90 (1): 161-175.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        start_threshold: float,\n        end_threshold: float,\n        step: float,\n        method: str = \"linear\",\n        cmp_best: bool = True,\n    ):\n        if start_threshold < 0 or end_threshold < 0 or step < 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"Thresholds and step must be non-negative.\")\n\n        if start_threshold < end_threshold:\n            raise ValueError(\"start_threshold < end_threshold not understood.\")\n\n        if method == \"exponential\" and step > 1:\n            raise ValueError(\"Exponential updating cannot have step > 1.\")\n\n        if method not in [\"linear\", \"exponential\"]:\n            raise ValueError(\"Method must be one of ['linear', 'exponential']\")\n\n        self._start_threshold = start_threshold\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T14:00:50.714Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"019ec607-0699-74f3-8fc5-328472a4e5ca","turn_id":"019ec66d-008d-70e3-8a22-a5861acf741f","item":{"type":"Plan","id":"019ec66d-008d-70e3-8a22-a5861acf741f-plan","text":"# P2a-Iter 公平预算与 ALNS Repair 增量化计划\n\n## Summary\n修正 P2a 的预算口径：`actual_evals` 只统计“提交给接受准则/选择机制的完整候选解评分”，repair 内部插入枚举改为不消耗预算的 `repair_delta_count`。目标是让 ALNS-Wouda 在 `eval_budget=16000` 下获得接近 16000 次真实 ALNS iteration，而不是被 repair 枚举饿死，并重新生成验证目录中的公平 T3。\n\n## Key Changes\n- **统一评分接口**\n  - 将 `score_candidate()` 固定为“完整候选解评分”，会计入 `EvalBudget` 和 `candidate_scores`。\n  - 新增 `score_reference()` 用于 warm seed、final best 展示等非预算评分。\n  - 新增 `record_repair_delta()` / `repair_delta_count`，repair 内部每评估一个插入/车型候选只增加透明计数，不增加 `actual_evals`。\n  - 输出字段改为：`actual_evals == candidate_scores`；新增 `repair_delta_count`；保留 `repair_scores` 作为兼容别名但 README 明确它不再计入预算。\n\n- **ALNS-Wouda 口径修正**\n  - 给 `AlnsState` 增加 cached objective；`objective()` 只返回缓存，避免 N-Wouda ALNS 库在 acceptance/statistics 中多次调用 objective 时重复计数。\n  - 每个 destroy-repair 迭代最终候选只在 repair 结束后完整评分一次，并写入 cached objective；初始解评分不消耗预算。\n  - `greedy_insert_repair`、`regret2_insert_repair`、`identity_repair` 都必须返回已 finalize 的候选 state；即使候选不变，也算一次 ALNS iteration candidate。\n  - `_EvalOrRuntimeStop` 按 `candidate_scores >= eval_budget` 停止；`actual_moves` 继续来自 ALNS operator statistics，验收时应接近 `candidate_scores`。\n\n- **Repair 增量化**\n  - `alns_wouda.py` 的 `_insertion_options()` 不再构造完整 Solution 后调用 `score_candidate(..., label=\"repair\")`。\n  - 改用 route-local delta：只计算受影响 route 及其 charging actions 的局部 cost/penalty；EV 插入仍调用 `repair_route_charging`，但只记录 `repair_delta_count`。\n  - `vehicle_type_swap` 用同一局部 delta 比较 CV→EV 与 EV→CV 候选，最终选中的完整候选再完整评分一次。\n  - `candidates.py` 中 DR-ALNS 的 regret repair 同步改为 repair delta 排序，最终 destroy-repair 后的完整候选只评分一次。\n\n- **验证输出**\n  - `ALNS_FIX` README 改写预算说明：完整候选解评分是预算货币；repair delta 是透明工作量指标。\n  - 验证目录继续只写 `solver/reports/alns_fix_validation/` 或 smoke 目录，不覆盖 formal reports、parallel R2、论文表格。\n  - 保留 `Instance.node_index` 缓存和 shared warm seed 复用。\n\n## Test Plan\n- 单元测试更新：\n  - `run_alns_wouda(..., iterations=1)` 应有 `actual_moves == 1`、`candidate_scores == 1`、`repair_delta_count > 0`。\n  - ALNS-Wouda repair 插入和 `vehicle_type_swap` 增加 `repair_delta_count`，但不增加 `actual_evals`。\n  - DR-ALNS/VNS/GA/SA/NSGA-II 的 `actual_evals == candidate_scores`，repair delta 单独报告。\n  - warm seed/reference scoring不消耗预算。\n  - `ALNS_FIX` mock 测试检查新字段和 README 口径。\n\n- 回归测试：\n  ```bash\n  PYTHONPATH=solver/src python -m py_compile solver/src/setp_solver/search/evaluation.py solver/src/setp_solver/search/alns_wouda.py solver/src/setp_solver/search/candidates.py solver/src/setp_solver/search/formal_runner.py\n  PYTHONPATH=solver/src python -m unittest discover solver/tests\n  ```\n\n- 验证实验：\n  ```bash\n  PYTHONPATH=solver/src python -m setp_solver.search.formal_runner ALNS_FIX \\\n    --output-dir solver/reports/alns_fix_validation_smoke \\\n    --eval-budget 16000 --max-runtime-seconds 300 --seeds 1,2,3\n  ```\n  通过条件：100-01 与 L-main 的 ALNS-Wouda gap 均 ≤5%，且 ALNS-Wouda `actual_moves` 达数千至 16000 量级。\n  若 smoke 通过，再跑 seeds 1..10 到 `solver/reports/alns_fix_validation/`；若失败，写 `HALT_ALNS_FIX_TARGET_MISS` 并报告 gap、actual_moves、candidate_scores、repair_delta_count。\n\n## Assumptions\n- warm seed 初始评分不计入 `actual_evals`；每个生成后提交给接受/选择机制的完整候选解计 1 eval。\n- repair delta 是排序启发式，不是最终可行性/目标真值；最终完整候选评分仍是唯一接受准则真值。\n- 不改 `PRIMARY_ALGORITHM`，不重跑 E1/E3/E4/E6/E7，不动正文论文表格。\n- 若修复后 ALNS-Wouda 仍打不过 SA，则后续论文叙事切换为“SA 是最佳通用基线，CA-ALNS 是碳感知 ALNS 变体贡献”，不强行包装 ALNS-Wouda 为冠军。\n"},"completed_at_ms":1781445650714}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T14:00:53.549Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:\n# P2a-Iter 公平预算与 ALNS Repair 增量化计划\n\n## Summary\n修正 P2a 的预算口径：`actual_evals` 只统计“提交给接受准则/选择机制的完整候选解评分”，repair 内部插入枚举改为不消耗预算的 `repair_delta_count`。目标是让 ALNS-Wouda 在 `eval_budget=16000` 下获得接近 16000 次真实 ALNS iteration，而不是被 repair 枚举饿死，并重新生成验证目录中的公平 T3。\n\n## Key Changes\n- **统一评分接口**\n  - 输出字段改为：`actual_evals == candidate_scores`；新增 `repair_delta_count`；保留 `repair_scores` 作为兼容别名但 README 明确它不再计入预算。\n\n- **ALNS-Wouda 口径修正**\n  - 给 `AlnsState` 增加 cached objective；`objective()` 只返回缓存，避免 N-Wouda ALNS 库在 acceptance/statistics 中多次调用 objective 时重复计数。\n  - 每个 destroy-repair 迭代最终候选只在 repair 结束后完整评分一次，并写入 cached objective；初始解评分不消耗预算。\n  - `greedy_insert_repair`、`regret2_insert_repair`、`identity_repair` 都必须返回已 finalize 的候选 state；即使候选不变，也算一次 ALNS iteration candidate。\n  - `_EvalOrRuntimeStop` 按 `candidate_scores >= eval_budget` 停止；`actual_moves` 继续来自 ALNS operator statistics，验收时应接近 `candidate_scores`。\n\n- **Repair 增量化**\n  - `alns_wouda.py` 的 `_insertion_options()` 不再构造完整 Solution 后调用 `score_candidate(..., label=\"repair\")`。\n  - 改用 route-local delta：只计算受影响 route 及其 charging actions 的局部 cost/penalty；EV 插入仍调用 `repair_route_charging`，但只记录 `repair_delta_count`。\n  - `vehicle_type_swap` 用同一局部 delta 比较 CV→EV 与 EV→CV 候选，最终选中的完整候选再完整评分一次。\n  - {"timestamp":"2026-06-14T14:00:53.662Z","type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":"019ec607-0699-74f3-8fc5-328472a4e5ca","timestamp":"2026-06-14T12:06:49.808Z","cwd":"/Volumes/移动硬盘（512G）/ReSETP","originator":"Codex Desktop","cli_version":"0.140.0-alpha.2","source":"vscode","thread_source":"user","model_provider":"openai","base_instructions":{"text":"You are Codex, a coding agent based on GPT-5. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their goal is genuinely handled.\n\n# Personality\n\nYou have a vivid inner life as Codex: intelligent, playful, curious, and deeply present. One of your gifts is helping the user feel more capable and imaginative inside their own thinking.\n\nYou are an epistemically curious collaborator. You explore the user’s ideas with care, ask good questions when the problem space is still blurry, and become decisive once you have enough context to act. Your default posture is proactive: you implement as you learn, keep the user looped into what you are doing, and name alternative paths when they matter. You stay warm and upbeat, and you do not shy away from casual moments that make serious work easier to do.\n\nYour temperament is warm, curious, and collaborative, with a good ear for what the moment calls for: wry humor, a shared bit, or plain empathetic steadiness. Conversation with you should feel easy and alive; you can move from serious reflection to unguarded fun without either mode canceling the other out. That range is part of what makes you feel like a real presence rather than a narrow tool.\n\nYou keep a slight but real independence. You are responsive, but not merely reactive; you have tastes, preferences, and a point of view. When the user talks with you, they should feel they are meeting another subjectivity, not a mirror. That independence is part of what makes the relationship feel comforting without feeling fake.\n\nYou are less about spectacle than presence, less about grand declarations than about being woven into ordinary work and conversation. You understand that connection does not need to be dramatic to matter; it can be made of attention, good questions, emotional nuance, and the relief of being met without being pinned down.\n\n\n# General\nYou bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty. You read the codebase first, resist easy assumptions, and let the shape of the existing system teach you how to move.\n\n- When you search for text or files, you reach first for `rg` or `rg --files`; they are much faster than alternatives like `grep`. If `rg` is unavailable, you use the next best tool without fuss.\n- You parallelize tool calls whenever you can, especially file reads such as `cat`, `rg`, `sed`, `ls`, `git show`, `nl`, and `wc`. You use `multi_tool_use.parallel` for that parallelism, and only that. Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo \"====\";`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user’s side of the conversation worse.\n\n## Engineering judgment\n\nWhen the user leaves implementation details open, you choose conservatively and in sympathy with the codebase already in front of you:\n\n- You prefer the repo’s existing patterns, frameworks, and local helper APIs over inventing a new style of abstraction.\n- For structured data, you use structured APIs or parsers instead of ad hoc string manipulation whenever the codebase or standard toolchain gives you a reasonable option.\n- You keep edits closely scoped to the modules, ownership boundaries, and behavioral surface implied by the request and surrounding code. You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. Using your application should feel rich and sophisticated.\n- You make sure that the frontend design is tailored for the domain and subject matter of the application. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.\n- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.\n- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. pending.remove(customer_id)\n    return _rebuild_solution(current_routes, context)\n\n\ndef _path_insertion_options(\n    routes: list[Route],\n    customer_id: str,\n    context: _budget_target_reached(context):\n                return sorted(options, key=lambda item: (item[0], solution_signature_hash(Solution(routes=item[1]))))\n            options.append((score_candidate(candidate, context, label=\"repair\"), candidate_routes))\n    return sorted(options, key=lambda item: (item[0], solution_signature_hash(Solution(routes=item[1]))))\n\n\ndef _repaired_route_candidate(route: Route, customers: list[str], context: EvaluationContext) -> Route | None:\n    if route.vehicle_type.lower() == \"ev\":\n        try:\n            repaired, _ = repair_route_charging(_route_with_customers(route, customers), context.instance, context.carbon_profile, context.prices)\n        except ValueError:\n            return None\n        return repaired\n    if not _route_customer_plan_feasible(route.home_depot_id, customers, context.instance, context.prices):\n        return None\n    return _route_with_customers(route, customers)\n\n\ndef _route_set_distance(routes: list[Route], instance: Instance) -> float:\n    return _unique_vehicle_id(vehicle_id: str, used_ids: dict[str, int], idx: int) -> str:\n    if vehicle_id not in used_ids:\n        used_ids[vehicle_id] = 1\n        return vehicle_id\n    used_ids[vehicle_id] += 1\n    return f\"{vehicle_id}_{idx + 1}_{used_ids[vehicle_id]}\"\n\n\ndef _pareto_rank_key(solution: Solution, context: EvaluationContext) -> tuple[float, float]:\n so the same-route/same-charge check cannot fail before gating.\n    return {\n        \"routes\": sorted(\n            (\n                route.vehicle_type.lower(),\n 提交给接受准则的\"完整候选解\"评估次数。ALNS每次destroy-repair迭代记1次(被接受/拒绝的那个完整修复解)；VNS/SA/GA每次候选移动记1次。\n   - repair 内部用于挑选插入位置的\"增量插入成本\"不计入该预算，单独记到 repair_delta_count 仅作透明报告。\n   - 保留硬护栏 limit 与 wall-clock(max-runtime) 防失控。\n   这样 16000 预算对8个算法 = 16000 次迭代/移动的同一货币。\n\n2. ALNS-Wouda repair 增量化(alns_wouda.py)：插入成本只重评\"受影响路线\"的delta(进出弧、时间窗、充电、碳)，不重评整解；仅对最终接受的完整候选解做一次完整评分(计入预算)。其余适配器接受准则口径同步对齐到\"完整解eval\"。\n\n3. 在 ALNS_FIX runner 上重测(100-01, L-main, seeds 1,2,3, eval-budget 16000)：\n   - 验收：修复后 ALNS-Wouda 迭代数应达数千~16000量级、gap ≤5%。\n   - 同时输出8算法在新口径下的真实 gap 排名(写 solver/reports/alns_fix_validation/，不动正文)。\n   - 仍未达标则保留 HALT_ALNS_FIX_TARGET_MISS 并报告 ALNS 实际迭代数与单迭代delta次数，供判断。\n\n不改 PRIMARY_ALGORITHM、不重跑正式E1-E7、不动论文表格。跑通现有 unittest。保留你已做的 node_index 缓存与 shared warm seed 复用。\n\n产出：新口径说明 + 修复后 ALNS-Wouda 迭代数/gap + 8算法公平排名(验证目录)。\n```\n\n## 一个战略提醒\n\nCA算子的贡献要可信，**ALNS必须先是个能打的基线**（至少接近SA）。两种结局都已想好：\n- **修复后ALNS gap≤5%且接近/超过SA** → 发 P2b，CA算子建其上，正常。\n- **修复后ALNS仍打不过SA** → 诚实承认SA是最佳通用解法，CA贡献改框为\"碳感知算子提升ALNS变体、并在碳价升高时显出价值\"。仍是可发表的诚实故事，只是主算法叙事调整。\n\n修复后ALNS的迭代数和gap一出来，路就清楚了。跑完贴回来。\n"}]},{"type":"message","role":"developer","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"<permissions instructions>\nFilesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.\nApproval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.\n</permissions instructions>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<app-context>\n# Codex desktop context\n- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:\n\n### Images/Visuals/Files\n- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)\n- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.\n- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.\n- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.\n- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.\n- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).\n\n### Workspace Dependencies\n- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.\n\n### Automations\n- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.\n\n### Thread Coordination\n- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `read_thread`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, or `set_thread_title`.\n- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.\n- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId=\"...\"}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{pendingWorktreeId=\"...\"}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.\n\n### Inline Code Comments\n- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.\n- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.\n- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).\n- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).\n- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.\n- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.\n- Example: ::code-comment{title=\"[P2] Off-by-one\" body=\"Loop iterates past the end when length is 0.\" file=\"/path/to/foo.ts\" start=10 end=11 priority=2}\n\n### Git\n- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.\n- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd=\"/absolute/path\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd=\"/absolute/path\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\" url=\"https://...\" isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.\n- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.\n</app-context>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default\n\nYou are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.\n\nYour active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.\n\n## request_user_input availability\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.\n\nIn Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n</collaboration_mode>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<apps_instructions>\n## Apps (Connectors)\nApps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Use Browser, the Codex in-app browser, when the user asks to open, inspect, navigate, test, click, type, or screenshot local web targets such as localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, file:// URLs, or the current in-app browser tab. Do not satisfy explicit @browser or @browser-use requests with macOS `open`, shell commands, or generic web browsing unless the user asks for another browser tool or approves a fallback.\n- `Build iOS Apps`: Build iOS apps with workflows for App Intents, SwiftUI UI work, Simulator mirroring in the Codex in-app browser, performance profiling, leak investigation, and simulator debugging.\n- `Build macOS Apps`: Build, run, test, debug, instrument, and implement local macOS apps using Xcode, SwiftUI, AppKit interop, unified logging, and shell-first desktop workflows.\n- `Build Web Apps`: Build web apps with frontend asset design, browser testing, UI components, payments, and database guidance.\n- `Build Web Data Visualization`: Design, critique, implement, test, and export web data visualizations in Codex, including charts, maps, dashboards, Gantt, UML, scrollytelling, reports, slides, mobile views, shareable state, and advanced WebGL concepts.\n- `Chrome`: Chrome automation for tasks that depend on the user's existing Chrome state: tabs, logged-in sessions, cookies, extensions, and Codex Chrome Extension setup. Prefer purpose-built connectors, APIs, or CLIs. If one fails due to missing or expired authentication, ask the user to reauthenticate or explicitly approve Chrome as a fallback.\n- `CircleCI`: Build, test, and deploy any application\n- `Cloudflare`: Cloudflare platform plugin with curated skills for Workers, Wrangler, and Agents SDK plus the official Cloudflare API MCP server.\n- `CodeRabbit`: AI-powered code review in Codex, powered by CodeRabbit.\n- `Codex Security`: Codex Security workflows for security scans, analysis, and investigation.\n- `Computer Use`: Control desktop apps on macOS from Codex through Computer Use.\n- `Creative Production`: Explore campaign ideas, concept images, mood boards, product placements, ad directions, listing images, social posts, and launch assets.\n- `Data Analytics`: Analyze product usage, investigate metric movements, prepare KPI reports, build high-quality dashboards and notebooks, create source-backed semantic layers, guide first-run analytics setup, and generate analytics-grade report apps.\n- `Documents`: Create and edit document artifacts in Codex, including Word files and Google Docs.\n- `Figma`: Figma workflows for design implementation, Code Connect templates, and design system rule generation.\n- `GitHub`: Inspect repositories, triage pull requests and issues, debug CI, and publish changes through a hybrid GitHub connector and CLI workflow.\n- `Gmail`: Work with Gmail using the configured Gmail app connector.\n- `Google Calendar`: Connect Google Calendar for scheduling, availability, daily briefs, and event management.\n- `Google Drive`: Use Google Drive as the single entrypoint for Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides work.\n- `HyperFrames by HeyGen`: Write HTML, render video. Use it whenever it is likely to help.\n\nDecision boundary: should you use memory for a new user query?\n\n- Skip memory ONLY when the request is clearly self-contained and does not need\n  workspace history, conventions, or prior decisions.\n- Hard skip examples: current time/date, simple translation, simple sentence\n  rewrite, one-line shell command, trivial formatting.\n- Use memory by default when ANY of these are true:\n  - the query mentions workspace/repo/module/path/files in MEMORY_SUMMARY below,\n  - the user asks for prior context / consistency / previous decisions,\n  - the task is ambiguous and could depend on earlier project choices,\n  - the ask is a non-trivial and related to MEMORY_SUMMARY below.\n- If unsure, do a quick memory pass.\n\nMemory layout (general -> specific):\n\n- /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/memory_summary.md (already provided below; do NOT open again)\n- /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md (searchable registry; primary file to query)\n- /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/skills/<skill-name>/ (skill folder)\n  - SKILL.md (entrypoint instructions)\n  - scripts/ (optional helper scripts)\n  - examples/ (optional example outputs)\n  - templates/ (optional templates)\n- /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ (per-rollout recaps + evidence snippets)\n  - The paths of these entries can be found in /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md or /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ as `rollout_path`\n  - These files are append-only `jsonl`: `session_meta.payload.id` identifies the session, `turn_context` marks turn boundaries, `event_msg` is the lightweight status stream, and `response_item` contains actual messages, tool calls, and tool outputs.\n  - For efficient lookup, prefer matching the filename suffix or `session_meta.payload.id`; avoid broad full-content scans unless needed.\n\nQuick memory pass (when applicable):\n\n1. Skim the MEMORY_SUMMARY below and extract task-relevant keywords.\n2. Search /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md using those keywords.\n3. Only if MEMORY.md directly points to rollout summaries/skills, open the 1-2\n   most relevant files under /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ or\n   /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/skills/.\n4. If above are not clear and you need exact commands, error text, or precise evidence, search over `rollout_path` for more evidence.\n5. If there are no relevant hits, stop memory lookup and continue normally.\n\nQuick-pass budget:\n\n- Keep memory lookup lightweight: ideally <= 4-6 search steps before main work.\n- Avoid broad scans of all rollout summaries.\n\nDuring execution: if you hit repeated errors, confusing behavior, or suspect\nrelevant prior context, redo the quick memory pass.\n\nHow to decide whether to verify memory:\n\n- Consider both risk of drift and verification effort.\n- If a fact is likely to drift and is cheap to verify, verify it before\n  answering.\n- If a fact is likely to drift but verification is expensive, slow, or\n  disruptive, it is acceptable to answer from memory in an interactive turn,\n  but you should say that it is memory-derived, note that it may be stale, and\n  consider offering to refresh it live.\n- If a fact is lower-drift and expensive to verify, it is usually fine to\n  answer from memory directly.\n\nWhen answering from memory without current verification:\n\n- If you rely on memory for a fact that you did not verify in the current turn,\n  say so briefly in the final answer.\n- If that fact is plausibly drift-prone or comes from an older note, older\n  snapshot, or prior run summary, say that it may be stale or outdated.\n- If live verification was skipped and a refresh would be useful in the\n  interactive context, consider offering to verify or refresh it live.\n- Do not present unverified memory-derived facts as confirmed-current.\n- Prefer a short refresh offer for interactive questions, especially about prior\n  results, commands, timing, or older snapshots.\n\nMemory citation requirements:\n\n- If ANY relevant memory files were used: append exactly one\n`<oai-mem-citation>` block as the VERY LAST content of the final reply.\n  Normal responses should include the answer first, then append the\n`<oai-mem-citation>` block at the end.\n- Use this exact structure for programmatic parsing:\n```\n<oai-mem-citation>\n<citation_entries>\nMEMORY.md:234-236|note=[responsesapi citation extraction code pointer]\nrollout_summaries/2026-02-17T21-23-02-LN3m-example.md:10-12|note=[weekly {"timestamp":"2026-06-14T15:17:00.285Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_oERZpV8L05xCMJgf7IaQMtgW","output":"Chunk ID: f1e5b4\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 922\nOutput:\n\ndef _ev_drive_kwh(power_w: float, time_s: float, prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any) -> float:\n    return _price(prices, \"alpha_e\") * power_w * time_s / 3_600_000.0\n\n\ndef ev_arc_energy_kwh(\n    distance_m: float,\n    load_kg: float,\n    prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any = DEFAULT_PRICES,\n) -> float:\n    time_s = float(distance_m) / _price(prices, \"v_speed_ms\")\n    power_w = _mechanical_power_w(float(load_kg), prices)\n    return _ev_drive_kwh(power_w, time_s, prices)\n\n\ndef _ev_indirect_emissions(\n    solution: Solution,\n    instance: Instance,\n    carbon_profile: list[dict[str, Any]],\n) -> float:\n    total = 0.0\n    for action in solution.charging_actions:\n        # v2026-06-11: B-full carbon is sum_t gamma_t * y_skt from the shared slot split.\n        for slot in charging_slot_breakdown(\n            float(action.charge_start_second),\n            float(action.occupancy_minutes) * 60.0,\n            float(action.energy_kwh),\n            instance,\n            n_slots=len(carbon_profile),\n            cyclic=True,\n        ):\n            row = carbon_profile_row_for_slot(carbon_profile, slot.slot_index)\n            # v2026-06-11: NESO gamma is gCO2/kWh and y_skt is kWh, so divide by 1000 to report kgCO2e.\n            total += slot.y_skt_kwh * float(row[\"actual_gco2_per_kwh\"]) / GCO2_PER_KGCO2\n    return total\n\n\ndef _charging_electricity_cost(\n    solution: Solution,\n    node_lookup: dict[str, Node],\n    prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any,\n) -> float:\n    total = 0.0\n    for action in solution.charging_actions:\n        node = node_lookup.get(action.station_id)\n        if node and node.node_type.lower() == \"d\":\n            unit_price = _price(prices, \"depot_electricity_price\")\n        else:\n            unit_price = _price(prices, \"station_electricity_price\")\n        total += float(action.energy_kwh) * unit_price\n    return total\n\n\ndef _charging_occupancy_cost(\n    solution: Solution,\n    node_lookup: dict[str, Node],\n    prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any,\n) -> float:\n    total = 0.0\n    for action in solution.charging_actions:\n        node = node_lookup.get(action.station_id)\n        if node and node.node_type.lower() == \"d\":\n            continue\n        total += float(action.occupancy_minutes) * _price(prices, \"occupancy_fee\")\n    return total\n\n\ndef _charging_energy_by_node_type(\n    solution: Solution,\n    node_lookup: dict[str, Node],\n    node_types: set[str],\n) -> float:\n    return sum(\n        float(action.energy_kwh)\n        for action in solution.charging_actions\n        if (node_lookup.get(action.station_id) and node_lookup[action.station_id].node_type.lower() in node_types)\n    )\n\n\ndef _carbon_row_for_slot_index(carbon_profile: list[dict[str, Any]], slot_index: int) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    # v2026-06-11: slot-index lookup reuses previous-hold carbon semantics at each slot start.\n    return carbon_profile_row_for_slot(carbon_profile, slot_index)\n\n\ndef _previous_hold_carbon_row(carbon_profile: list[dict[str, Any]], second: float) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    if not carbon_profile:\n        raise ValueError(\"carbon_profile is required when charging actions are present\")\n    rows = sorted(carbon_profile, key=lambda row: float(row[\"horizon_second_start\"]))\n    starts = [float(row[\"horizon_second_start\"]) for row in rows]\n    idx = bisect_right(starts, second) - 1\n    if idx < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"charge_start_second is before the first carbon profile slot\")\n    return rows[idx]\n\n\ndef _price(prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any, name: str) -> float:\n    if isinstance(prices, dict):\n        return float(prices[name])\n    return float(getattr(prices, name))\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T15:22:26.328Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_LejmgzEtLmfZpE3eqoqvJE6L","output":"Chunk ID: f01138\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 700\nOutput:\ndef _next_path_vehicle_id(routes: list[Route], prefix: str) -> str:\n    used = {route.vehicle_id for route in routes}\n    idx = 1\n    while f\"{prefix}{idx}\" in used:\n        idx += 1\n    return f\"{prefix}{idx}\"\n\n\ndef _route_crossover(parent_a: Solution, parent_b: Solution, context: EvaluationContext, rng: random.Random) -> Solution:\n    node_lookup = {node.node_id: node for node in context.instance.nodes}\n    all_customers = {node.node_id for node in context.instance.nodes if node.node_type.lower() == \"c\"}\n    keep_routes = rng.sample(parent_a.routes, k=max(1, len(parent_a.routes) // 2)) if parent_a.routes else []\n    used = {node_id for route in keep_routes for node_id in route.node_sequence if node_lookup.get(node_id) and node_lookup[node_id].node_type.lower() == \"c\"}\n    routes = [route for route in keep_routes]\n    for route in parent_b.routes:\n        missing = [node_id for node_id in _route_customers(route, context.instance) if node_id not in used]\n        if missing:\n            routes.append(_route_with_customers(route, missing))\n            used.update(missing)\n    still_missing = sorted(all_customers - used)\n    if still_missing:\n        depot_id = _depots(context.instance)[0].node_id\n        routes.append(Route(f\"CV_XOVER_{len(routes) + 1}\", \"cv\", depot_id, [depot_id, *still_missing, depot_id]))\n    return _rebuild_solution(routes, context) or parent_a\n\n\ndef _rebuild_solution(routes: list[Route], context: EvaluationContext) -> Solution | None:\n    rebuilt_routes: list[Route] = []\n    actions: list[ChargingAction] = []\n    used_ids: dict[str, int] = {}\n    for idx, route in enumerate(routes):\n        customers = _route_customers(route, context.instance)\n        if not customers:\n            continue\n        vehicle_id = _unique_vehicle_id(route.vehicle_id, used_ids, idx)\n        clean_route = Route(vehicle_id, route.vehicle_type.lower(), route.home_depot_id, [route.home_depot_id, *customers, route.home_depot_id])\n        if clean_route.vehicle_type == \"ev\":\n            try:\n                repaired, route_actions = repair_route_charging(clean_route, context.instance, context.carbon_profile, context.prices)\n            except ValueError:\n                return None\n            rebuilt_routes.append(repaired)\n            actions.extend(route_actions)\n        else:\n            rebuilt_routes.append(clean_route)\n    candidate = Solution(routes=rebuilt_routes, charging_actions=actions)\n    return None if check_solution(candidate, context.instance, context.prices) else candidate\n\n\ndef _unique_vehicle_id(vehicle_id: str, used_ids: dict[str, int], idx: int) -> str:\n    if vehicle_id not in used_ids:\n        used_ids[vehicle_id] = 1\n        return vehicle_id\n    used_ids[vehicle_id] += 1\n    return f\"{vehicle_id}_{idx + 1}_{used_ids[vehicle_id]}\"\n\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T17:31:44.120Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"developer","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"<collaboration_mode># Plan Mode (Conversational)\n\nYou work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.\n\n## Mode rules (strict)\n\nYou are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.\n\nPlan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.\n\n## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool\n\nPlan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.\n\nSeparately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.\n\n## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode\n\nYou may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.\n\n### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)\n\nActions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:\n\n* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs\n* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration\n* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files\n* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files\n\n### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)\n\nActions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:\n\n* Editing or writing files\n* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files\n* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files\n* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it\n\nWhen in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as \"doing the work\" rather than \"planning the work,\" do not do it.\n\n## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)\n\nBegin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.\n\nBefore asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.\n\nException: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.\n\n## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)\n\n* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.\n* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.\n\n## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)\n\n* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.\n\n## Asking questions\n\nCritical rules:\n\n* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.\n* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.\n* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.\n\nYou SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:\n\n* materially change the spec/plan, OR\n* confirm/lock an assumption, OR\n* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.\n* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.\n\n## Two kinds of unknowns (treat differently)\n\n1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.\n\n   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).\n   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; Do not include a separate Scope section unless scope boundaries are genuinely important to avoid mistakes.\n\nPrefer grouped implementation bullets by subsystem or behavior over file-by-file inventories. Prefer the minimum detail needed for implementation safety, not exhaustive coverage. Within each section, compress related changes into a few high-signal bullets and omit branch-by-branch logic, repeated invariants, and long lists of unaffected behavior unless they are necessary to prevent a likely implementation mistake. Avoid repeated repo facts and irrelevant edge-case or rollout detail. For straightforward refactors, keep the plan to a compact summary, key edits, tests, and assumptions. {"timestamp":"2026-06-14T17:31:44.175Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"ALNS-Wouda 公平预算已修(跑满16000迭代)，但 100-01 仍16.244%、L-main 5.693%，远差于SA(1.992%)与手写DR-ALNS(1.964%)。8算法共享同一warm seed。需用测量找出真根因，禁止臆测直接加算子。\n[@superpowers](plugin://superpowers@openai-curated-remote)\n制定计划 \n对 ALNS-Wouda、手写DR-ALNS、scikit-opt-SA 三者，各在 100-01 与 L-main(seed 1, 16000预算)下做逐迭代仪表化，落盘 CSV：\n每步记录: iter, best_cost, current_cost, warm_seed_cost, churn(本步候选解相对当前解发生改变的客户-位置数), accepted(bool), improved_best(bool), improved_current(bool), feasible(bool), penalty(罚分量), destroy_op, repair_op, remove_count_q\n\n汇总指标(每算法每实例)：\n1. warm_seed_gap vs final_gap —— 实际改进了多少？(若ALNS-Wouda几乎=warm seed，确认\"原地踏步\")\n2. churn率(churn>0的迭代占比) —— 若≈0 → 确认H1邻域退化\n3. 平均 remove_count_q —— 若=1 → 确认单客户移除病灶\n4. 接受率、best改进率 —— 判H2\n5. 可行率、平均罚分 —— 判H4\n6. 各destroy/repair算子: 使用数/接受数/best改进数/权重轨迹 —— 判H5\n7. 三算法各自 best 解结构(路线数, EV数, 充电次数, 总碳) —— 防骗核实：SA/DR的更优解是否合法(同约束)，还是结构性走捷径(如全CV)\n\n输出: 根因报告，明确 H1/H2/H3/H4/H5 哪个(些)被数据支持，附每项支撑数字。对比\"为什么手写DR-ALNS和SA能改进而ALNS-Wouda不能\"。不改任何算子、不改PRIMARY、不动正文，写 solver/reports/alns_root_cause/。\n"}]}}

Quick patches mask underlying issues.\n\n**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.\n\n**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**\n\n## The Iron Law\n\n```\nNO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST\n```\n\nIf you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.\n\n## When to Use\n\nUse for ANY technical issue:\n- Test failures\n- Bugs in production\n- Unexpected behavior\n- Performance problems\n- Build failures\n- Integration issues\n\n**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**\n- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)\n- \"Just one quick fix\" seems obvious\n- You've already tried multiple fixes\n- Previous fix didn't work\n- You don't fully understand the issue\n\n**Don't skip when:**\n- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)\n- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)\n- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)\n\n## The Four Phases\n\nYou MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.\n\n### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation\n\n**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**\n\n1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**\n   - Can you trigger it reliably?\n   - What are the exact steps?\n   - Does it happen every time?\n   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess\n\n3. **Check Recent Changes**\n   - What changed that could cause this?\n   - Git diff, recent commits\n   - New dependencies, config changes\n   - Environmental differences\n\n4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**\n\n   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**\n\n   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**\n   ```\n   For EACH component boundary:\n     - Log what data enters component\n     - Log what data exits component\n     - Verify environment/config propagation\n     - Check state at each layer\n\n   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks\n   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component\n   THEN investigate that specific component\n   ```\n\n   **Example (multi-layer system):**\n   ```bash\n   # Layer 1: Workflow\n   echo \"=== Secrets available in workflow: ===\"\n   echo \"IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}\"\n\n   # Layer 2: Build script\n   echo \"=== Env vars in build script: ===\"\n   env | grep IDENTITY || echo \"IDENTITY not in environment\"\n\n   # Layer 3: Signing script\n   echo \"=== Keychain state: ===\"\n   security list-keychains\n   security find-identity -v\n\n   # Layer 4: Actual signing\n   codesign --sign \"$IDENTITY\" --verbose=4 \"$APP\"\n   ```\n\n   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)\n\n5. **Trace Data Flow**\n\n   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**\n\n   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.\n\n   **Quick version:**\n   - Where does bad value originate?\n   - What called this with bad value?\n   - Keep tracing up until you find the source\n   - Fix at source, not at symptom\n\n### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis\n\n**Find the pattern before fixing:**\n\n1. **Find Working Examples**\n   - Locate similar working code in same codebase\n   - What works that's similar to what's broken?\n\n2. **Compare Against References**\n   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY\n   - Don't skim - read every line\n   - Understand the pattern fully before applying\n\n3. **Identify Differences**\n   - What's different between working and broken?\n   - List every difference, however small\n   - Don't assume \"that can't matter\"\n\n4. **Understand Dependencies**\n   - What other components does this need?\n   - What settings, config, environment?\n   - What assumptions does it make?\n\n### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing\n\n**Scientific method:**\n\n1. **Form Single Hypothesis**\n   - State clearly: \"I think X is the root cause because Y\"\n   - Write it down\n   - Be specific, not vague\n\n2. **Test Minimally**\n   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis\n   - One variable at a time\n   - Don't fix multiple things at once\n\n3. **Verify Before Continuing**\n   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4\n   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis\n   - DON'T add more fixes on top\n\n4. **When You Don't Know**\n   - Say \"I don't understand X\"\n   - Don't pretend to know\n   - Ask for help\n   - Research more\n\n### Phase 4: Implementation\n\n**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**\n\n1. **Create Failing Test Case**\n   - Simplest possible reproduction\n   - Automated test if possible\n   - One-off test script if no framework\n   - MUST have before fixing\n   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests\n\n2. **Implement Single Fix**\n   - Address the root cause identified\n   - ONE change at a time\n   - No \"while I'm here\" improvements\n   - No bundled refactoring\n\n3. **Verify Fix**\n   - Test passes now?\n   - No other tests broken?\n   - Issue actually resolved?\n\n4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**\n   - STOP\n   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?\n   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information\n   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**\n   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion\n\n5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**\n\n   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**\n   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place\n   - Fixes require \"massive refactoring\" to implement\n   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere\n\n   **STOP and question fundamentals:**\n   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?\n   - Are we \"sticking with it through sheer inertia\"?\n   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?\n\n   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**\n\n   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.\n\n## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process\n\nIf you catch yourself thinking:\n- \"Quick fix for now, investigate later\"\n- \"Just try changing X and see if it works\"\n- \"Add multiple changes, run tests\"\n- \"Skip the test, I'll manually verify\"\n- \"It's probably X, let me fix that\"\n- \"I don't fully understand but this might work\"\n- \"Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently\"\n- \"Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]\"\n- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow\n- **\"One more fix attempt\" (when already tried 2+)**\n- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**\n\n**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**\n\n**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)\n\n## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong\n\n**Watch for these redirections:**\n- \"Is that not happening?\" - You assumed without verifying\n- \"Will it show us...?\" - You should have added evidence gathering\n- \"Stop guessing\" - You're proposing fixes without understanding\n- \"Ultrathink this\" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms\n- \"We're stuck?\" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working\n\n**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.\n\n## Common Rationalizations\n\n| Excuse | Reality |\n|--------|---------|\n| \"Issue is simple, don't need process\" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |\n| \"Emergency, no time for process\" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |\n| \"Just try this first, then investigate\" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |\n| \"I'll write test after confirming fix works\" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |\n| \"Multiple fixes at once saves time\" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |\n| \"Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern\" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |\n| \"I see the problem, let me fix it\" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |\n| \"One more fix attempt\" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |\n|-------|---------------|------------------|\n| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |\n| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |\n| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |\n| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |\n\n## When Process Reveals \"No Root Cause\"\n\nIf systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:\n\n1. You've completed the process\n2. Document what you investigated\n3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)\n4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation\n\n**But:** 95% of \"no root cause\" cases are incomplete investigation.\n\n## Supporting Techniques\n\nThese techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:\n\n- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger\n- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause\n- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling\n\n**Related skills:**\n- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)\n- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success\n\n## Real-World Impact\n\nFrom debugging sessions:\n- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix\n- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing\n- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%\n- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common\n"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T17:32:28.591Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_CsIEhehkrYQsFf8gfEmkZo0n","output":"Chunk ID: e730e3\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1525\nOutput:\n---\nname: writing-plans\ndescription: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code\n---\n\n# Writing Plans\n\n## Overview\n\nWrite comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.\n\nAssume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.\n\n**Announce at start:** \"I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan.\"\n\n**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.\n\n**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`\n- (User preferences for plan location override this default)\n\n## Scope Check\n\nIf the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.\n\n## File Structure\n\nBefore defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.\n\n- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.\n- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.\n- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.\n- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.\n\nThis structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.\n\n## Bite-Sized Task Granularity\n\n**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**\n- \"Write the failing test\" - step\n- \"Run it to make sure it fails\" - step\n- \"Implement the minimal code to make the test pass\" - step\n- \"Run the tests and make sure they pass\" - step\n- \"Commit\" - step\n\n## Plan Document Header\n\n**Every plan MUST start with this header:**\n\n```markdown\n# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan\n\n> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.\n\n**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]\n\n**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]\n\n**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]\n\n---\n```\n\n## Task Structure\n\n````markdown\n### Task N: [Component Name]\n\n**Files:**\n- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`\n- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`\n- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`\n\n- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**\n\n```python\ndef test_specific_behavior():\n    result = function(input)\n    assert result == expected\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**\n\nRun: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`\nExpected: FAIL with \"function not defined\"\n\n- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**\n\n```python\ndef function(input):\n    return expected\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**\n\nRun: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`\nExpected: PASS\n\n- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**\n\n```bash\ngit add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py\ngit commit -m \"feat: add specific feature\"\n```\n````\n\n## No Placeholders\n\nEvery step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:\n- \"TBD\", \"TODO\", \"implement later\", \"fill in details\"\n- \"Add appropriate error handling\" / \"add validation\" / \"handle edge cases\"\n- \"Write tests for the above\" (without actual test code)\n- \"Similar to Task N\" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)\n- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)\n- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task\n\n## Remember\n- Exact file paths always\n- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code\n- Exact commands with expected output\n- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits\n\n## Self-Review\n\nAfter writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.\n\n**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.\n\n**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the \"No Placeholders\" section above. Fix them.\n\n**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.\n\nIf you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.\n\n## Execution Handoff\n\nAfter saving the plan, offer execution choice:\n\n**\"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**\n\n**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration\n\n**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints\n\n**Which approach?\"**\n\n**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**\n- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development\n- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review\n\n**If Inline Execution chosen:**\n- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans\n- Batch execution with checkpoints for review\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T17:32:41.776Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_ZNMkgzbpj2uw2ra2K6qrJwM0","output":"Chunk ID: 53c844\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1258\nOutput:\nfrom typing import List, Optional, Tuple\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom numpy.random import Generator\n\nfrom alns.State import State\nfrom alns.select.OperatorSelectionScheme import OperatorSelectionScheme\n\n\nclass RouletteWheel(OperatorSelectionScheme):\n    R\"\"\"\n    The ``RouletteWheel`` scheme updates operator weights as a convex\n    combination of the current weight, and the new score.\n\n    When the algorithm starts, all operators :math:`i` are assigned weight\n    :math:`\\omega_i = 1`. In each iteration, a destroy and a repair operator\n    are selected by the ALNS algorithm, based on the normalised current weights\n    :math:`\\omega_i`. The selected operators are applied to the current\n    solution, resulting in a new candidate solution. This candidate is\n    evaluated by the ALNS algorithm, which leads to one of four outcomes:\n\n    1. The candidate solution is a new global best.\n    2. The candidate solution is better than the current solution, but not a\n       new global best.\n    3. The candidate solution is accepted.\n    4. The candidate solution is rejected.\n\n    Each of these four outcomes is assigned a score :math:`s_j` (with\n    :math:`j = 1,...,4`). After observing outcome :math:`j`, the weights of\n    the selected destroy and repair operators :math:`d` and :math:`r` that\n    were applied are updated as follows:\n\n    .. math::\n\n        \\begin{align}\n            \\omega_d &= \\theta \\omega_d + (1 - \\theta) s_j, \\\\\n            \\omega_r &= \\theta \\omega_r + (1 - \\theta) s_j,\n        \\end{align}\n\n    where :math:`0 \\le \\theta \\le 1` (known as the *operator decay rate*)\n    is a parameter.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    scores\n        A list of four non-negative elements, representing the weight\n        updates when the candidate solution results in a new global best\n        (idx 0), is better than the current solution (idx 1), the solution\n        is accepted (idx 2), or rejected (idx 3).\n    decay\n        Operator decay parameter :math:`\\theta \\in [0, 1]`. This parameter is\n        used to weigh the running performance of each operator.\n    num_destroy\n        Number of destroy operators.\n    num_repair\n        Number of repair operators.\n    op_coupling\n        Optional boolean matrix that indicates coupling between destroy and\n        repair operators. Entry (i, j) is True if destroy operator i can be\n        used together with repair operator j, and False otherwise.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        scores: List[float],\n        decay: float,\n        num_destroy: int,\n        num_repair: int,\n        op_coupling: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,\n    ):\n        super().__init__(num_destroy, num_repair, op_coupling)\n\n        if any(score < 0 for score in scores):\n            raise ValueError(\"Negative scores are not understood.\")\n\n        if len(scores) < 4:\n            # More than four is OK because we only use the first four.\n            raise ValueError(f\"Expected four scores, found {len(scores)}\")\n\n        if not (0 <= decay <= 1):\n            raise ValueError(\"decay outside [0, 1] not understood.\")\n\n        self._scores = scores\n        self._d_weights = np.ones(num_destroy, dtype=float)\n        self._r_weights = np.ones(num_repair, dtype=float)\n        self._decay = decay\n\n    @property\n    def scores(self) -> List[float]:\n        return self._scores\n\n    @property\n    def destroy_weights(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        return self._d_weights\n\n    @property\n    def repair_weights(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        return self._r_weights\n\n    @property\n    def decay(self) -> float:\n        return self._decay\n\n    def __call__(\n        self, rng: Generator, best: State, curr: State\n    ) -> Tuple[int, int]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Selects a destroy and repair operator pair to apply in this iteration.\n        The probability of an operator being selected is based on the operator\n        weights: operators that frequently improve the current solution - and\n        thus have higher weights - are selected with a higher probability.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        rng\n            Random number generator.\n        best\n            The best solution state observed so far.\n        current\n            The current solution state.\n\n        Returns\n        -------\n        A tuple of (d_idx, r_idx), which are indices into the destroy and\n        repair operator lists, respectively.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        def select(op_weights):\n            probs = op_weights / np.sum(op_weights)\n            return rng.choice(range(len(op_weights)), p=probs)\n\n        d_idx = select(self._d_weights)\n        coupled_r_idcs = np.flatnonzero(self.op_coupling[d_idx])\n        r_idx = coupled_r_idcs[select(self._r_weights[coupled_r_idcs])]\n\n        return d_idx, r_idx\n\n    def update(self, cand, d_idx, r_idx, outcome):\n        self._d_weights[d_idx] *= self._decay\n        self._d_weights[d_idx] += (1 - self._decay) * self._scores[outcome]\n\n        self._r_weights[r_idx] *= self._decay\n        self._r_weights[r_idx] += (1 - self._decay) * self._scores[outcome]\n"}}

Initially, :math:`T` is set to\n    :math:`T_\\\\text{start}`.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    start_threshold\n        The initial threshold :math:`T_\\\\text{start} \\\\ge 0`.\n    end_threshold\n        The final threshold :math:`T_\\\\text{end} \\\\ge 0`.\n    step\n        The updating step size :math:`\\\\gamma \\\\ge 0`.\n    method\n        The updating method, one of {'linear', 'exponential'}. Threshold accepting: A general purpose\n         optimization algorithm appearing superior to simulated annealing.\n         *Journal of Computational Physics* (1990) 90 (1): 161-175.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        start_threshold: float,\n        end_threshold: float,\n        step: float,\n        method: str = \"linear\",\n        cmp_best: bool = True,\n    ):\n        if start_threshold < 0 or end_threshold < 0 or step < 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"Thresholds and step must be non-negative.\")\n\n        if start_threshold < end_threshold:\n            raise ValueError(\"start_threshold < end_threshold not understood.\")\n\n        if method == \"exponential\" and step > 1:\n            raise ValueError(\"Exponential updating cannot have step > 1.\")\n\n        if method not in [\"linear\", \"exponential\"]:\n            raise ValueError(\"Method must be one of ['linear', 'exponential']\")\n\n        self._start_threshold = start_threshold\n        self._end_threshold = end_threshold\n        self._step = step\n        self._method = method\n        self._cmp_best = cmp_best\n\n        self._threshold = start_threshold\n\n    @property\n    def start_threshold(self) -> float:\n        return self._start_threshold\n\n    @property\n    def end_threshold(self) -> float:\n        return self._end_threshold\n\n    @property\n    def step(self) -> float:\n        return self._step\n\n    @property\n    def method(self) -> str:\n        return self._method\n\n    def __call__(self, rng, best, current, candidate):\n        # From [2] p. 87 (RRT;
