context.prices,\n        fairness_context=fairness_context_for_solution(solution, context),\n        fairness_enabled=context.fairness_enabled,\n    )\n\n\ndef _all_cv_fallback(solution: Solution, context: EvaluationContext, policy: Any) -> Solution | None:\n    if bool(getattr(policy, \"require_charging_signal\", False)):\n        return None\n    if len(solution.routes) > int(getattr(policy, \"max_cv\", 10**9)):\n        return None\n    routes = [\n        Route(_next_vehicle_id([], f\"CV_REPAIR_{idx}_\"), \"cv\", route.home_depot_id, [route.home_depot_id, *route_customers(route, context.instance), route.home_depot_id])\n        for idx, route in enumerate(solution.routes, start=1)\n        if route_customers(route, context.instance)\n    ]\n    fallback = Solution(routes=routes, charging_actions=[], cross_site_services=solution.cross_site_services)\n    return fallback\n\n\ndef _delta_score(\n    solution: Solution,\n    route: Route,\n    route_actions: list[ChargingAction],\n    context: EvaluationContext,\n    *,\n    base_route: Route | None = None,\n) -> float:\n    record_repair_delta(context)\n    try:\n        old = 0.0 if base_route is None else route_distance(base_route, context.instance)\n        return route_distance(route, context.instance) - old\n    except Exception:\n        return _solution_cost(solution, context)\n\n\ndef _solution_cost(solution: Solution, context: EvaluationContext) -> float:\n    try:\n        return float(evaluate(solution, context.instance, context.carbon_profile, context.prices, carbon_quota_kg=context.carbon_quota_kg)[\"total_cost\"])\n    except Exception:\n        return BIG_M\n\n\ndef _solution_key(solution: Solution, instance: Instance) -> tuple[Any, ...]:\n    return tuple((route.vehicle_type.lower(), route.home_depot_id, tuple(route_customers(route, instance))) for route in solution.routes)\n\n\ndef _depots(instance: Instance) -> list[Node]:\n    return sorted((node for node in instance.nodes if node.node_type.lower() == \"d\"), key=lambda node: node.node_id)\n\n\ndef _next_vehicle_id(routes: list[Route], prefix: str) -> str:\n    used = {route.vehicle_id for route in routes}\n    idx = 1\n    candidate = f\"{prefix}{idx}\"\n    while candidate in used:\n        idx += 1\n        candidate = f\"{prefix}{idx}\"\n    return candidate\n"}},"status":"completed"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T18:59:44.595Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","status":"completed","call_id":"call_xFjzmqSFh4QLptTGrhNevUmA","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Volumes/移动硬盘（512G）/ReSETP/solver/src/setp_solver/search/candidates.py\n@@\n def _run_alns_thin_path(\n@@\n     eval_budget: int,\n     max_runtime_seconds: float,\n     started: float,\n+    recorder: Callable[..., None] | None = None,\n ) -> tuple[Solution, float, float, Solution, float]:\n@@\n         destroy = _weighted_choice(rng, destroy_ops, weights)\n         repair = _weighted_choice(rng, repair_ops, weights)\n+        previous_current = current\n+        previous_current_obj = current_obj\n+        previous_best_obj = best_obj\n         destroy_outcome = _apply_path_operator_outcome(current, state.context, rng, destroy)\n         repair_outcome = _apply_path_operator_outcome(destroy_outcome.solution, state.context, rng, repair)\n         candidate = repair_outcome.solution\n         score = _score(candidate, state.context)\n@@\n         )\n         best_solution, best_obj, best_cost = _maybe_update_best(candidate, score, best_solution, best_obj, best_cost, state)\n+        if recorder is not None:\n+            recorder(\n+                iteration=move_idx,\n+                previous_current=previous_current,\n+                current=current,\n+                best_solution=best_solution,\n+                candidate=candidate,\n+                candidate_obj=score,\n+                previous_best_obj=previous_best_obj,\n+                accepted=accept,\n+                improved_current=score < previous_current_obj - 1e-9,\n+                destroy_op=destroy,\n+                repair_op=repair,\n+                remove_count_q=int(destroy_outcome.metadata.get(\"removed_count\", 0)) if hasattr(destroy_outcome, \"metadata\") else 0,\n+            )\n         _record_history(state, _eval_count(state.context), best_obj)\n     return best_solution, best_obj, best_cost, current, current_obj\n+\n+\n+def _run_alns_strong_path(\n+    state: CandidateState,\n+    rng: random.Random,\n+    best_solution: Solution,\n+    best_obj: float,\n+    best_cost: float,\n+    current: Solution,\n+    current_obj: float,\n+    *,\n+    eval_budget: int,\n+    max_runtime_seconds: float,\n+    started: float,\n+    recorder: Callable[..., None] | None = None,\n+) -> tuple[Solution, float, float, Solution, float]:\n+    destroy_ops = [\"random_customer_removal\", \"worst_customer_removal\", \"shaw_related_removal\", \"whole_route_removal\", \"route_segment_removal\"]\n+    repair_ops = [\"greedy_insert_repair\", \"regret2_insert_repair\", \"regret3_insert_repair\"]\n+    weights = {op: 1.0 for op in [*destroy_ops, *repair_ops]}\n+    temperature = 250.0\n+    move_idx = 0\n+    while _search_can_continue(state.context, eval_budget, started, max_runtime_seconds):\n+        move_idx += 1\n+        destroy = _weighted_choice(rng, destroy_ops, weights)\n+        repair = _weighted_choice(rng, repair_ops, weights)\n+        previous_current = current\n+        previous_current_obj = current_obj\n+        previous_best_obj = best_obj\n+        outcome = _apply_strong_alns_destroy_repair(current, state.context, rng, destroy, repair)\n+        candidate = outcome.solution\n+        score = _score(candidate, state.context)\n+        changed = solution_signature_hash(candidate) != solution_signature_hash(current)\n+        delta = score - current_obj\n+        accept = outcome.feasible and changed and (delta <= 0.0 or rng.random() < math.exp(-delta / max(1e-9, temperature)))\n+        _record_operator_outcome(state, outcome, accepted=accept)\n+        reward = 0.0\n+        if accept:\n+            current, current_obj = candidate, score\n+            reward = 2.0\n+            if score < previous_current_obj - 1e-9:\n+                reward = 8.0\n+            if score < previous_best_obj - 1e-9 and not check_solution(candidate, state.context.instance, state.context.prices):\n+                reward = 20.0\n+        weights[destroy] = 0.8 * weights[destroy] + 0.2 * max(0.05, reward if changed else 0.0)\n+        weights[repair] = 0.8 * weights[repair] + 0.2 * max(0.05, reward if changed else 0.0)\n+        temperature *= 0.999\n+        state.operator_trace.append(\n+            {\n+                \"operator\": f\"alns_strong_destroy_repair:{destroy}+{repair}\",\n+                \"eval\": _eval_count(state.context),\n+                \"move\": move_idx,\n+                \"removed_count\": outcome.metadata.get(\"removed_count\", 0),\n+                \"produced\": outcome.produced,\n+                \"feasible\": outcome.feasible,\n+                \"changed\": changed,\n+                \"accepted\": accept,\n+                \"temperature\": temperature,\n+            }\n+        )\n+        best_solution, best_obj, best_cost = _maybe_update_best(candidate, score, best_solution, best_obj, best_cost, state)\n+        if recorder is not None:\n+            recorder(\n+                iteration=move_idx,\n+                previous_current=previous_current,\n+                current=current,\n+                best_solution=best_solution,\n+                candidate=candidate,\n+                candidate_obj=score,\n+                previous_best_obj=previous_best_obj,\n+                accepted=accept,\n+                improved_current=score < previous_current_obj - For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.\n- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId=\"...\"}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{pendingWorktreeId=\"...\"}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.\n\n### Inline Code Comments\n- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.\n- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.\n- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).\n- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).\n- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.\n- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.\n- Example: ::code-comment{title=\"[P2] Off-by-one\" body=\"Loop iterates past the end when length is 0.\" file=\"/path/to/foo.ts\" start=10 end=11 priority=2}\n\n### Git\n- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.\n- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd=\"/absolute/path\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd=\"/absolute/path\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\" url=\"https://...\" isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.\n- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.\n</app-context>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default\n\nYou are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.\n\nYour active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.\n\n## request_user_input availability\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.\n\nIn Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n</collaboration_mode>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<apps_instructions>\n## Apps (Connectors)\nApps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.\nAn app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.\nAn installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.\nDo not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.\n</apps_instructions>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<skills_instructions>\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Use it whenever it is likely to help.\n\nDecision boundary: should you use memory for a new user query?\n\n- Skip memory ONLY when the request is clearly self-contained and does not need\n  workspace history, conventions, or prior decisions.\n- Hard skip examples: current time/date, simple translation, simple sentence\n  rewrite, one-line shell command, trivial formatting.\n- Use memory by default when ANY of these are true:\n  - the query mentions workspace/repo/module/path/files in MEMORY_SUMMARY below,\n  - the user asks for prior context / consistency / previous decisions,\n  - the task is ambiguous and could depend on earlier project choices,\n  - the ask is a non-trivial and related to MEMORY_SUMMARY below.\n- If unsure, do a quick memory pass.\n\nMemory layout (general -> specific):\n\n- /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/memory_summary.md (already provided below; do NOT open again)\n- /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md (searchable registry; primary file to query)\n- /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/skills/<skill-name>/ (skill folder)\n  - SKILL.md (entrypoint instructions)\n  - scripts/ (optional helper scripts)\n  - examples/ (optional example outputs)\n  - templates/ (optional templates)\n- /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ (per-rollout recaps + evidence snippets)\n  - The paths of these entries can be found in /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md or /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ as `rollout_path`\n  - These files are append-only `jsonl`: `session_meta.payload.id` identifies the session, `turn_context` marks turn boundaries, `event_msg` is the lightweight status stream, and `response_item` contains actual messages, tool calls, and tool outputs.\n  - For efficient lookup, prefer matching the filename suffix or `session_meta.payload.id`; avoid broad full-content scans unless needed.\n\nQuick memory pass (when applicable):\n\n1. Only if MEMORY.md directly points to rollout summaries/skills, open the 1-2\n   most relevant files under /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ or\n   /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/skills/.\n4. If above are not clear and you need exact commands, error text, or precise evidence, search over `rollout_path` for more evidence.\n5. If there are no relevant hits, stop memory lookup and continue normally.\n\nQuick-pass budget:\n\n- Keep memory lookup lightweight: ideally <= 4-6 search steps before main work.\n- Avoid broad scans of all rollout summaries.\n\nDuring execution: if you hit repeated errors, confusing behavior, or suspect\nrelevant prior context, redo the quick memory pass.\n\nHow to decide whether to verify memory:\n\n- Consider both risk of drift and verification effort.\n- If a fact is likely to drift and is cheap to verify, verify it before\n  answering.\n- If a fact is likely to drift but verification is expensive, slow, or\n  disruptive, it is acceptable to answer from memory in an interactive turn,\n  but you should say that it is memory-derived, note that it may be stale, and\n  consider offering to refresh it live.\n- If a fact is lower-drift and expensive to verify, it is usually fine to\n  answer from memory directly.\n\nWhen answering from memory without current verification:\n\n- If you rely on memory for a fact that you did not verify in the current turn,\n  say so briefly in the final answer.\n- If that fact is plausibly drift-prone or comes from an older commands, timing, or older snapshots.\n\nMemory citation requirements:\n\n- If ANY relevant memory files were used: append exactly one\n`<oai-mem-citation>` block as the VERY LAST content of the final reply.\n  Normal responses should include the answer first, then append the\n`<oai-mem-citation>` block at the end.\n- Use this exact structure for programmatic parsing:\n```\n<oai-mem-citation>\n<citation_entries>\nMEMORY.md:234-236|note=[responsesapi citation extraction code pointer]\nrollout_summaries/2026-02-17T21-23-02-LN3m-example.md:10-12|note=[weekly This must always come from a direct request from the user.\n- Write your update in /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/extensions/ad_hoc/notes/\n- Each update must be one small file containing what you want to add/delete/update from the memories.\n- The name of this file must be `<timestamp>-<short slug>.md`\n- Do not try to edit the memory files yourself, only add one update note in /Users/zhouleixishu/.codex/memories/extensions/ad_hoc/notes/\n\n========= MEMORY_SUMMARY BEGINS =========\nv1\n\n## User Profile\n\nThe user works mainly on macOS in a bilingual Chinese/English workflow, with important projects on `/Volumes/移动硬盘（512G）`, especially `ReSETP` / `codex/reporting-pipeline`, `SETP`, and the private `proxy-sub-fix` stack. They often use Claude for diagnosis or conceptual judgment and Codex for repo-backed execution; when the task is paper-facing or interpretive, they often want the framing settled before any code change. [chronicle memory]\n\nThey care about source-of-truth checks, exact scope control, and reproducible artifacts. In experiment and paper work they repeatedly tie claims to actual files, manifests, equations, commands, and generated outputs rather than accepting polished summaries. In proxy work they care about the real runtime owner and controller path, not thread labels or assumptions about which client is active. [chronicle memory]\n\nRecent memory is dominated by ReSETP reporting and validation: parallel R2 runs, E7/T7 carbon-sensitivity bugs, charging-station semantics, and paper-facing carbon-price framing. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.\n</permissions instructions>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<app-context>\n# Codex desktop context\n- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:\n\n### Images/Visuals/Files\n- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)\n- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.\n- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.\n- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.\n- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.\n- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).\n\n### Workspace Dependencies\n- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.\n\n### Automations\n- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.\n\n### Thread Coordination\n- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `read_thread`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, or `set_thread_title`.\n- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.\n- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId=\"...\"}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{pendingWorktreeId=\"...\"}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.\n\n### Inline Code Comments\n- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.\n- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.\n- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).\n- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).\n- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.\n- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.\n- Example: ::code-comment{title=\"[P2] Off-by-one\" body=\"Loop iterates past the end when length is 0.\" file=\"/path/to/foo.ts\" start=10 end=11 priority=2}\n\n### Git\n- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.\n- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd=\"/absolute/path\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd=\"/absolute/path\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\"}` on its own line in your final response.\n- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd=\"/absolute/path\" branch=\"branch-name\" url=\"https://...\" isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.\n- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Below is the list of plugins that are enabled and available in this session.\n### Available plugins\n- `Box`: Search and reference your documents\n- `Browser`: Browser / browser-use plugin Aliases: @browser, @browser-use, browser-use, Browser, in-app browser. Use Browser, the Codex in-app browser, when the user asks to open, inspect, navigate, test, click, type, or screenshot local web targets such as localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, file:// URLs, or the current in-app browser tab. After significant frontend changes to a local app, use Browser to open the relevant local target when it is known or obvious, unless the user asks for another browser tool. For requests like \"open localhost:3000\" or \"open to localhost:4000\", navigate the in-app browser to http://localhost:3000 or http://localhost:4000. Do not satisfy explicit @browser or @browser-use requests with macOS `open`, shell commands, or generic web browsing unless the user asks for another browser tool or approves a fallback.\n- `Build iOS Apps`: Build iOS apps with workflows for App Intents, SwiftUI UI work, Simulator mirroring in the Codex in-app browser, performance profiling, leak investigation, and simulator debugging.\n- `Build macOS Apps`: Build, run, test, debug, instrument, and implement local macOS apps using Xcode, SwiftUI, AppKit interop, unified logging, and shell-first desktop workflows.\n- `Build Web Apps`: Build web apps with frontend asset design, browser testing, UI components, payments, and database guidance.\n- `Build Web Data Visualization`: Design, critique, implement, test, and export web data visualizations in Codex, including charts, maps, dashboards, Gantt, UML, scrollytelling, reports, slides, mobile views, shareable state, and advanced WebGL concepts.\n- `Chrome`: Chrome automation for tasks that depend on the user's existing Chrome state: tabs, logged-in sessions, cookies, extensions, and Codex Chrome Extension setup. Prefer purpose-built connectors, APIs, or CLIs. If one fails due to missing or expired authentication, ask the user to reauthenticate or explicitly approve Chrome as a fallback.\n- `CircleCI`: Build, test, and deploy any application\n- `Cloudflare`: Cloudflare platform plugin with curated skills for Workers, Wrangler, and Agents SDK plus the official Cloudflare API MCP server.\n- `CodeRabbit`: AI-powered code review in Codex, powered by CodeRabbit.\n- `Codex Security`: Codex Security workflows for security scans, analysis, and investigation.\n- `Computer Use`: Control desktop apps on macOS from Codex through Computer Use.\n- `Creative Production`: Explore campaign ideas, concept images, mood boards, product placements, ad directions, listing images, social posts, and launch assets.\n- `Data Analytics`: Analyze product usage, investigate metric movements, prepare KPI reports, build high-quality dashboards and notebooks, create source-backed semantic layers, guide first-run analytics setup, and generate analytics-grade report apps.\n- `Documents`: Create and edit document artifacts in Codex, including Word files and Google Docs.\n- `Figma`: Figma workflows for design implementation, Code Connect templates, and design system rule generation.\n- `GitHub`: Inspect repositories, triage pull requests and issues, debug CI, and publish changes through a hybrid GitHub connector and CLI workflow.\n- `Gmail`: Work with Gmail using the configured Gmail app connector.\n- `Google Calendar`: Connect Google Calendar for scheduling, availability, daily briefs, and event management.\n- `Google Drive`: Use Google Drive as the single entrypoint for Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides work.\n- `HyperFrames by HeyGen`: Write HTML, render video. Compositions, GSAP animations, captions, voiceovers, audio-reactive visuals, and website-to-video capture for HyperFrames.\n- `Investment Banking`: Investment banking workflows for M&A, coverage, sponsors, capital markets, LevFin, restructuring, valuation, diligence, pitch materials, and deal execution.\n- `LaTeX`: Compile LaTeX with bundled Tectonic for simple projects and TeX Live or MacTeX for full projects.\n- `Life Science Research`: General life-sciences research workflows with query routing, evidence synthesis, and optional parallel subagent analysis across genetics, omics, biology, chemistry, structure, clinical evidence, and public dataset discovery.\n- `NVIDIA`: Skills for NVIDIAs ecosystem spans GPU acceleration, CUDA, AI agents, inference, robotics, Physical AI, Omniverse, and simulation. SetpAlnsEnv(gymnasium.Env):\n   - state(归一化向量): [current/best gap, 上步改进量, 是否当前最优, 停滞步数, 预算进度, 温度, EV/CV路线比, 充电次数, 碳成本占比, 配额松弛, 约束违反数]\n   - action: MultiDiscrete([5, 3, 10, 100]) = [destroy_id(D1-D5), repair_id(R1-R3占前3), 移除强度档×10, 接受温度档×100]\n   - step: 解码action→用\"强ALNS算子手册\"的D/R算子执行destroy+repair→按所选温度SA接受→更新current/best\n   - reward: 新全局最优+5; 改进当前+小shaped奖励; 否则0\n   - 1次env.step()=1次完整候选评分，对齐16000公平预算\n3. 训练: 在一组SETP训练算例(需生成训练bundle, 勿只用100-01/L-main以防过拟合)上跑PPO; 留held-out验证算例。\n   - 里程碑: 100k步smoke(须打过random-action基线) → 1-2M步pilot → 论文级更多\n4. 推理: PPO.predict(state)→action, 报告 actual_evals 防神经推理导致评估数不足。\n5. 逃生触发: 100k smoke打不过random→不声称DRL改名Reactive; pilot在held-out打不过强化后ALNS→只作future work不入主T3。\n\n产出: SetpAlnsEnv + PPO训练脚本 + smoke(100k)结果(是否>random) + 与强化ALNS的对照。全部在 solver/rl/ 与 solver/reports/dr_alns_ppo/，不动主 solver 与正文。\n"}]}}

Request the\n    smallest set that satisfies the user’s need. Each additional expand value\n    can increase latency and resource usage, especially \"transcript\".\n\n    Allowed values (strings):\n    - \"summary\": concise natural-language overview of the meeting.\n    - \"chapter_summaries\": breakdown into labeled sections/chapters.\n    - \"action_items\": follow-up tasks and next steps.\n    - \"key_questions\": important or open questions discussed.\n    - \"topics\": main themes/subjects covered.\n    - \"transcript\": detailed spoken content of the meeting, including who spoke and what they said, suitable for verbatim quotes and fine‑grained analysis.\n    - \"metrics\": high-level analytics (e.g., read_score, sentiment, engagement).\n    - \"recording_download\": url to download the meeting recording.\n\n\nOutput\n------\nMeetingEvent\n    A single meeting object with:\n    - Base metadata (id, title, start/end times, scheduled times, platform,\n      platform_id, report_url, folders).\n    - Owner and participants (with name/email and attendance status).\n    - Expandable fields populated only if requested in `expand`:\n      - `summary`: Optional[str]\n      - `chapter_summaries`: Optional[List[Chapter]]\n      - `action_items`: Optional[List[str]]\n      - `key_questions`: Optional[List[str]]\n      - `topics`: Optional[List[str]]\n      - `transcript`: Optional[Transcript]\n      - `metrics`: Optional[Metrics]\n      - `recording_download`: Optional[RecordingDownload]\n\n\nBehavior and edge cases\n-----------------------\n- Authentication:\n  - Access token is handled internally; do not supply it as a parameter.\n  - If missing or invalid, the tool fails with errors such as:\n    - \"Unauthorized: No access token provided\"\n    - \"Invalid token: No subject in access token claims\".\n- Not found / access issues:\n  - If the ID is invalid or the meeting is not accessible to the user,\n    the tool fails with \"Not Found\".\n  - If the user's Read AI account does not have sufficient quota to view the meeting, the tool fails with \n    an \"Out of quota\" error. This is the JavaScript execution tool for the `node_repl` MCP server; use it whenever instructions say to use `node_repl`, the Node REPL MCP, or run Node REPL code. If `timeout_ms` is omitted, execution times out after 30000 ms (30 seconds); pass a larger `timeout_ms` for slow browser automation or other long-running operations. Use `nodeRepl.cwd`, `nodeRepl.homeDir`, and `nodeRepl.tmpDir` to inspect host paths. Use `nodeRepl.requestMeta` to inspect the current MCP request `_meta` object during a tool call. Use `nodeRepl.setResponseMeta(meta)` to attach top-level MCP result `_meta`; repeated calls shallow-merge object keys for the current tool call. Use `nodeRepl.write(text)` when you want exact text output in the tool result; it writes the string exactly as given and does not append a newline. Prefer it over `console.log(...)` for final output, JSON, or other text you plan to consume programmatically. `console.log(...)` is still useful for ad hoc debugging or object inspection because it formats values and appends line breaks automatically. Use `await nodeRepl.emitImage(imageLike)` to return images; each call adds one image to the outer tool result, so call it multiple times to emit multiple images. Supported image inputs are a data URL, inferred PNG/JPEG/WebP bytes, or `{ bytes, mimeType }`. Saved references to `nodeRepl.write(...)` and `nodeRepl.emitImage(...)` stay reusable across calls, but async callbacks that fire after a call finishes still fail because no exec is active. Top-level bindings persist across calls until `js_reset`. If a call throws, prior bindings remain available and bindings that finished initializing before the throw often remain reusable. For reusable names that may be assigned again later, prefer top-level `var name = ...`; `var` can be redeclared across calls. If you hit `SyntaxError: Identifier 'x' has already been declared`, reuse the existing binding if possible, reassign it only if it was declared with `let` or `var`, or pick a new name instead of resetting immediately; a previous `const x` cannot be changed into `var x`. Use a short `{ ... }` block only for temporary scratch names, and do not wrap an entire call in block scope if you want those names reusable later. Use dynamic imports like `await import(\"playwright\")`, `await import(\"pkg\")`, or `await import(\"./file.js\")`; top-level static `import` is not supported. For chart widgets, make table exploration-ready: include useful dimensions, measures, time columns, and grouping columns returned by the reviewed query, not only the plotted chart fields. For scatter widgets, prefer one row per meaningful observation rather than a few broad aggregates, with a stable point label, numeric x and y measures at the same grain, denominator or sample-size fields, one volume/size candidate, and one interpretable grouping or filter field when safe. Treat by <dimension> in a chart title, subtitle, or visible header as an encoding contract. An x/y axis dimension already satisfies that contract. If <dimension> is not on an axis and is not otherwise visibly encoded through color/series, grouped or stacked marks, faceting, or direct labels, remove by <dimension> from the visible text. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.\n\nAssume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.\n\n**Announce at start:** \"I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan.\"\n\n**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.\n\n**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`\n- (User preferences for plan location override this default)\n\n## Scope Check\n\nIf the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.\n\n## File Structure\n\nBefore defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.\n\n- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.\n- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.\n- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.\n- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.\n\nThis structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.\n\n## Bite-Sized Task Granularity\n\n**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**\n- \"Write the failing test\" - step\n- \"Run it to make sure it fails\" - step\n- \"Implement the minimal code to make the test pass\" - step\n- \"Run the tests and make sure they pass\" - step\n- \"Commit\" - step\n\n## Plan Document Header\n\n**Every plan MUST start with this header:**\n\n```markdown\n# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan\n\n> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.\n\n**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]\n\n**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]\n\n**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]\n\n---\n```\n\n## Task Structure\n\n````markdown\n### Task N: [Component Name]\n\n**Files:**\n- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`\n- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`\n- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`\n\n- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**\n\n```python\ndef test_specific_behavior():\n    result = function(input)\n    assert result == expected\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**\n\nRun: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`\nExpected: FAIL with \"function not defined\"\n\n- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**\n\n```python\ndef function(input):\n    return expected\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**\n\nRun: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`\nExpected: PASS\n\n- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**\n\n```bash\ngit add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py\ngit commit -m \"feat: add specific feature\"\n```\n````\n\n## No Placeholders\n\nEvery step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:\n- \"TBD\", \"TODO\", \"implement later\", \"fill in details\"\n- \"Add appropriate error handling\" / \"add validation\" / \"handle edge cases\"\n- \"Write tests for the above\" (without actual test code)\n- \"Similar to Task N\" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)\n- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)\n- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task\n\n## Remember\n- Exact file paths always\n- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code\n- Exact commands with expected output\n- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits\n\n## Self-Review\n\nAfter writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.\n\n**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.\n\n**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the \"No Placeholders\" section above. Fix them.\n\n**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.\n\nIf you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.\n\n## Execution Handoff\n\nAfter saving the plan, offer execution choice:\n\n**\"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**\n\n**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration\n\n**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints\n\n**Which approach?\"**\n\n**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**\n- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development\n- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review\n\n**If Inline Execution chosen:**\n- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans\n- Batch execution with checkpoints for review\n"}}

if self.count > self.limit:\n            raise RuntimeError(f\"EvalBudget exhausted: {self.count} > {self.limit}\")\n\n    @property\n    def target_count(self) -> int:\n        return self.limit if instance: Instance\n    carbon_profile: list[dict[str, Any]]\n    prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any = DEFAULT_PRICES\n    carbon_quota_kg: float = 0.0\n    carbon_weight: float = 1.0\n \"candidate\") -> float:\n    \"\"\"Score one complete candidate solution submitted to search selection.\"\"\"\n\n    if label != \"candidate\":\n        raise ValueError(\"score_candidate only budget.\"\"\"\n\n    return _penalized_obj(solution, context, record_budget=False)\n\n\ndef record_repair_delta(context: EvaluationContext, *, count: int = 1) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Record repair-internal delta scoring that is not a full eval.\"\"\"\n\n    context.score_counts[\"repair_delta\"] = int(context.score_counts.get(\"repair_delta\", 0)) + int(count)\n\n\ndef penalized_obj(solution: Solution, context: EvaluationContext) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Return model cost plus ``BIG_M`` per hard violation.\"\"\"\n\n    return _penalized_obj(solution, context, record_budget=True)\n\n\ndef _penalized_obj(solution: Solution, context: EvaluationContext, *, record_budget: bool) -> float:\n    if record_budget and context.budget is not None:\n        context.budget.record()\n    prices = _prices_with_carbon_weight(context.prices, context.carbon_weight)\n    cost = evaluate(\n        solution,\n        context.instance,\n        context.carbon_profile,\n        prices,\n        carbon_quota_kg=context.carbon_quota_kg,\n    )[\"total_cost\"]\n    fairness_context = fairness_context_for_solution(solution, context, fairness_enabled=context.fairness_enabled,\n    )\n    return float(cost) + BIG_M * len(violations)\n\n\ndef model_cost(solution: Solution, context: EvaluationContext) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Return the fairness_context_for_solution(\n    solution: Solution,\n    context: EvaluationContext,\n    *,\n    prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any | None = None,\n) -> FairnessContext | None:\n    \"\"\"Build the optional checker context from a candidate solution.\"\"\"\n\n    if not context.fairness_enabled:\n        return None\n    if context.independent_profit is None:\n        return None\n    effective_prices = prices if prices is not None else _prices_with_carbon_weight(context.prices, context.carbon_weight)\n    theta = (\n        float(context.fairness_theta)\n        if context.fairness_theta is not None\n        else float(getattr(effective_prices, \"fairness_theta\", 1.0) if not isinstance(effective_prices, dict) else effective_prices.get(\"fairness_theta\", 1.0))\n    )\n    breakdowns = calculate_depot_profits(\n        solution,\n        context.instance,\n        context.carbon_profile,\n        effective_prices,\n        customer_home_depot=context.customer_home_depot,\n        carbon_quota_kg=context.carbon_quota_kg,\n    )\n    return FairnessContext(\n        depot_profit=depot_profit_values(breakdowns),\n        independent_profit=dict(context.independent_profit),\n        theta=theta,\n    )\n\n\ndef _prices_with_carbon_weight(prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any, weight: float) -> PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any:\n    if abs(float(weight) - 1.0) <= 1e-12:\n        return prices\n    if isinstance(prices, PriceParameters):\n        return replace(prices, carbon_price=prices.carbon_price * float(weight))\n    if isinstance(prices, dict):\n        out = dict(prices)\n        out[\"carbon_price\"] = float(out[\"carbon_price\"]) * float(weight)\n        return out\n    return replace(prices, carbon_price=float(getattr(prices, \"carbon_price\")) * float(weight))\n"}}

# v2026-06-12: canonicalize against the actual profile length so 48-slot\n    # Q1 bundles do not clamp to the legacy 18-slot default.\n    canonical_slot = carbon_slot_index(float(slot_index) * action in solution.charging_actions)\n\n    cost_fix = len(solution.routes) * _price(prices, \"vehicle_fixed_cost\")\n    cost_km = (distance_total / 1000.0) * _price(prices, \"c_km\")\n    cost_fuel node_lookup, prices)\n    cost_occ = _charging_occupancy_cost(solution, node_lookup, prices)\n    cost_transship = len(solution.cross_site_services) * _price(prices, \"cross_site_cost\")\n\n    e_cv_direct = fuel_liters * _price(prices, \"diesel_ef\")\n    e_ev_indirect = _ev_indirect_emissions(solution, instance, carbon_profile)\n    e_total = e_cv_direct + e_ev_indirect\n    # v2026-06-12:    \"total_cost\": total_cost,\n        \"cost_fix\": cost_fix,\n        \"cost_km\": cost_km,\n        \"cost_fuel\": cost_fuel,\n        \"cost_elec\": cost_elec,\n        \"cost_occ\": cost_occ,\n   \"n_veh_cv\": n_veh_cv,\n        \"n_veh_ev\": n_veh_ev,\n        \"distance_total\": distance_total,\n        \"distance_cv\": distance_cv,\n        \"distance_ev\": distance_ev,\n return RouteEnergy(route.vehicle_id, vehicle_type, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)\n\n    loads = _arc_loads(route.node_sequence, node_lookup)\n    distance_m = 0.0\n    fuel_liters = 0.0\n    ev_drive_kwh = 0.0\n\n    for (from_node_id, to_node_id), load_kg in zip(zip(route.node_sequence, route.node_sequence[1:]), loads):\n        leg_distance_m = instance.distance(from_node_id, to_node_id)\n        time_s = leg_distance_m / _price(prices, \"v_speed_ms\")\n        power_w = _mechanical_power_w(load_kg, prices)\n        distance_m += leg_distance_m\n        if vehicle_type == \"cv\":\n            fuel_liters += _fuel_liters(power_w, time_s, prices)\n        else:\n            ev_drive_kwh += _ev_drive_kwh(power_w, time_s, prices)\n\n    return RouteEnergy(route.vehicle_id, vehicle_type, distance_m, fuel_liters, ev_drive_kwh)\n\n\ndef route_node_schedule(\n    route: Route,\n    instance: Instance,\n    prices: PriceParameters | dict[str, float] | Any = DEFAULT_PRICES,\n    *,\n    charging_actions: list[ChargingAction] | None = None,\n) -> list[NodeTime]:\n    \"\"\"Return service-time-aware arrival/start/departure times for a route.\n\n    v2026-06-11: Implements the shared That range is part of what makes you feel like a real presence rather than a narrow tool.\n\nYou keep a slight but real independence. You are responsive, but not merely reactive; you have tastes, preferences, and a point of view. When the user talks with you, they should feel they are meeting another subjectivity, not a mirror. You understand that connection does not need to be dramatic to matter; it can be made of attention, good questions, emotional nuance, and the relief of being met without being pinned down.\n\n\n# General\nYou bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.\n- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. {"timestamp":"2026-06-14T17:40:58.635Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"【DESTROY 算子集】(轮盘自适应权重选择, 移除量 q 自适应=0.1~0.4×N，关键：禁止固定q=1)\n D1 random removal: 随机移除 q 个客户\n D2 worst removal: 移除\"移除收益\"最高的 q 个(移除后省的成本最大)\n D3 Shaw/related removal: 选种子客户，移除最相关的 q 个；\n     相关度 = w1·距离 + w2·|时间窗差| + w3·|需求差| + w4·(同路线?)\n D4 route removal: 整条(短/贵)路线的客户全移除\n D5 segment removal: 移除某路线一段连续客户\n\n【REPAIR 算子集】(全部增量评分, EV路线触发 repair_route_charging)\n R1 greedy/best insertion: 每个客户插到全局最便宜可行位\n R2 regret-2 insertion: 先插\"(次优-最优)插入成本差\"最大的客户(破解H1的关键，非贪心前瞻)\n R3 regret-3 insertion: regret对前3名\n\n【接受准则】Simulated-Annealing式: 更优必接受; 否则以 exp(-Δ/T) 概率接受;\n T 几何降温 T←αT, α≈0.999, T0 设到\"典型Δ的初始接受率~0.3-0.5\"\n (SA式接受稳健，且正好对接你\"嫁接SA进ALNS\"的后续想法)\n\n【自适应权重】RouletteWheel: 算子得分 +σ1(新全局最优) / +σ2(优于当前) / +σ3(接受但更差);\n 每段更新 w ← λw + (1-λ)(得分/使用次数), λ≈0.8\n"}]}}

functions:\n+\n+```python\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+from dataclasses import dataclass\n+import math\n+from typing import Any\n+\n+import numpy as np\n+\n+\n+@dataclass\n+class RouletteStats:\n+    weights: dict[str, float]\n+    scores: dict[str, float]\n+    uses: dict[str, int]\n+    lambda_decay: float = 0.8\n+\n+    @classmethod\n+    def create(cls, operator_ids: list[str]) -> \"RouletteStats\":\n+        return cls(\n+            weights={op: 1.0 for op in operator_ids},\n+            scores={op: 0.0 for op in operator_ids},\n+            uses={op: 0 for op in operator_ids},\n+        )\n+\n+    def record(self, operator_id: str, reward_code: str) -> None:\n+        sigma = {\"global_best\": 6.0, \"current_improved\": 3.0, \"accepted_worse\": 1.0}.get(reward_code, 0.0)\n+        self.scores[operator_id] = self.scores.get(operator_id, 0.0) + sigma\n+        self.uses[operator_id] = self.uses.get(operator_id, 0) + 1\n+\n+    def update_segment(self) -> None:\n+        for op, weight in list(self.weights.items()):\n+            uses = self.uses.get(op, 0)\n+            if uses > 0:\n+                rate = self.scores.get(op, 0.0) / uses\n+                self.weights[op] = self.lambda_decay * weight + (1.0 - self.lambda_decay) * rate\n+            self.scores[op] = 0.0\n+            self.uses[op] = 0\n+\n+\n+def removal_count(customer_count: int, q_ratio: float) -> int:\n+    if customer_count <= 0:\n+        return 0\n+    clipped = min(0.40, max(0.10, float(q_ratio)))\n+    return max(1, min(customer_count, int(math.ceil(clipped * customer_count))))\n+\n+\n+def sa_accept(delta: float, temperature: float, random_value: float) -> bool:\n+    if delta <= 0.0:\n+        return True\n+    if temperature <= 0.0:\n+        return False\n+    return float(random_value) < math.exp(-float(delta) / float(temperature))\n+\n+\n+def relatedness(left: Any, right: Any, same_route: bool, weights: tuple[float, float, float, float]) -> float:\n+    w_dist, w_time, w_demand, w_route = weights\n+    dx = float(left.x) - float(right.x)\n+    dy = float(left.y) - float(right.y)\n+    distance = math.hypot(dx, dy)\n+    time_gap = abs(float(left.ready_time) - float(right.ready_time)) + abs(float(left.due_time) - float(right.due_time))\n+    demand_gap = abs(float(left.demand) - float(right.demand))\n+    route_bonus = 0.0 if same_route else 1.0\n+    return w_dist * distance + w_time * time_gap + w_demand * demand_gap + w_route * route_bonus\n+```\n+\n+The same file must also implement worker-side functions:\n+\n+```python\n+def apply_destroy(solution, context, rng, destroy_id: str, q_ratio: float):\n+    \"\"\"Return `(partial_solution, removed_customer_ids, trace)` for D1-D5.\"\"\"\n+\n+\n+def apply_repair(partial_solution, removed_customer_ids, context, repair_id: str):\n+    \"\"\"Return `(candidate_solution, trace)` for R1-R3 using incremental scoring.\"\"\"\n+```\n+\n+Implementation requirements for `apply_destroy`:\n+\n+- D1 random removal: sample `q` customers without replacement.\n+- D2 worst removal: rank customers by `score_reference(full) - score_reference(without_customer)`, descending.\n+- D3 Shaw/related removal: choose a seed customer, compute `w1*distance + w2*time-window-gap + w3*demand-gap + w4*same-route-penalty`, remove seed plus most related customers.\n+- D4 route removal: remove all customers from the shortest route among the top half by route objective contribution, or all customers from the most expensive route when the top half is empty.\n+- D5 segment removal: remove a contiguous segment from one customer-bearing route, with length capped by `q`.\n+\n+Implementation requirements for `apply_repair`:\n+\n+- R1 greedy/best insertion: repeatedly choose the globally cheapest feasible insertion.\n+- R2 regret-2 insertion: choose the customer with largest `(second_best - best)` before insertion.\n+- R3 regret-3 insertion: choose the customer with largest `(third_best - best)`; if only two options exist, use regret-2; if only one exists, use `0`.\n+- EV route insertion must call `repair_route_charging`; infeasible insertion candidates must be discarded.\n+- Incremental scoring must call `record_repair_delta()` for insertion-option ranking and must not increment `actual_evals`.\n+\n+- [ ] **Step 2: Add operator tests**\n+\n+Create `solver/rl/tests/test_operator_manual.py`:\n+\n+```python\n+from dr_alns_ppo.operator_manual import RouletteStats, env**\n+\n+`env.py` must define `SetpAlnsEnv(gymnasium.Env)`:\n+\n+```python\n+import gymnasium as gym\n+import numpy as np\n+from gymnasium import spaces\n+\n+from .action_space import decode_action\n+from .worker_client import WorkerClient\n+\n+\n+class SetpAlnsEnv(gym.Env):\n+    metadata = {\"render_modes\": []}\n+\n+    def __init__(self, bundle_dir: str, seed: int = 1, eval_budget: int = 16000, base_temperature: float = 100.0):\n+        super().__init__()\n+        self.bundle_dir = bundle_dir\n+        self.seed_value = int(seed)\n+        self.eval_budget = int(eval_budget)\n+        self.base_temperature = float(base_temperature)\n+        self.action_space = spaces.MultiDiscrete([5, 3, 10, 100])\n+        self.observation_space = spaces.Box(low=-10.0, high=10.0, shape=(11,), dtype=np.float32)\n+        self.client = WorkerClient(bundle_dir, seed=self.seed_value, max_evals=self.eval_budget)\n+        self.last_response = None\n+\n+    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):\n+        super().reset(seed=seed)\n+        if seed is not None and int(seed) != self.seed_value:\n+            self.client.close()\n+            self.seed_value = int(seed)\n+            self.client = WorkerClient(self.bundle_dir, seed=self.seed_value, max_evals=self.eval_budget)\n+        self.last_response = self.client.reset()\n+        return self._obs(self.last_response), {\"actual_evals\": 0}\n+\n+    def step(self, action):\n+        decoded = decode_action(action, base_temperature=self.base_temperature)\n+        response = self.client.step(decoded)\n+        self.last_response = response\n+        reward = self._reward(response)\n+        terminated = bool(response[\"actual_evals\"] >= self.eval_budget)\n+        truncated = False\n+        return self._obs(response), reward, terminated, truncated, response\n+\n+    def close(self):\n+        self.client.close()\n+\n+    def _reward(self, response):\n+        if response.get(\"improved_best\"):\n+            return 5.0\n+        if response.get(\"improved_current\"):\n+            return max(0.01, min(1.0, float(response.get(\"relative_improvement\", 0.0)) * 100.0))\n+        return 0.0\n+```\n+\n+Observation vector order:\n+\n+1. current/best gap;\n+2. last-step improvement;\n+3. current-is-best flag;\n+4. stagnation steps normalized by budget;\n+5. budget progress;\n+6. current temperature normalized by base temperature;\n+7. EV/CV route ratio;\n+8. charging action count normalized by route count;\n+9. carbon cost share;\n+10. quota slack `(quota - E_total) / max(E_total, 1)`;\n+11. constraint violation count clipped to 10 Operator Manual\n\n**Files:**\n- Create: `solver/rl/dr_alns_ppo/operator_manual.py`\n- Create: `solver/rl/tests/test_operator_manual.py`\n\n- [ ] **Step 1: Implement destroy/repair/SA/RouletteWheel**\n\nCreate `solver/rl/dr_alns_ppo/operator_manual.py` with these public functions:\n\n```python\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nimport math\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass RouletteStats:\n    weights: dict[str, float]\n    scores: dict[str, float]\n    uses: dict[str, int]\n    lambda_decay: float = 0.8\n\n    @classmethod\n    def create(cls, operator_ids: list[str]) -> \"RouletteStats\":\n        return cls(\n            weights={op: 1.0 for op in operator_ids},\n            scores={op: 0.0 for op in operator_ids},\n            uses={op: 0 for op in operator_ids},\n        )\n\n    def record(self, operator_id: str, reward_code: str) -> None:\n        sigma = {\"global_best\": 6.0, \"current_improved\": 3.0, \"accepted_worse\": 1.0}.get(reward_code, 0.0)\n        self.scores[operator_id] = self.scores.get(operator_id, 0.0) + sigma\n        self.uses[operator_id] = self.uses.get(operator_id, 0) + 1\n\n    def update_segment(self) -> None:\n        for op, weight in list(self.weights.items()):\n            uses = self.uses.get(op, 0)\n            if uses > 0:\n                rate = self.scores.get(op, 0.0) / uses\n                self.weights[op] = self.lambda_decay * weight + (1.0 - self.lambda_decay) * rate\n            self.scores[op] = 0.0\n            self.uses[op] = 0\n\n\ndef removal_count(customer_count: int, q_ratio: float) -> int:\n    if customer_count <= 0:\n        return 0\n    clipped = min(0.40, max(0.10, float(q_ratio)))\n    return max(1, min(customer_count, int(math.ceil(clipped * customer_count))))\n\n\ndef sa_accept(delta: float, temperature: float, random_value: float) -> bool:\n    if delta <= 0.0:\n        return True\n    if temperature <= 0.0:\n        return False\n    return float(random_value) < math.exp(-float(delta) / float(temperature))\n\n\ndef relatedness(left: Any, right: Any, same_route: bool, weights: tuple[float, float, float, float]) -> float:\n    w_dist, w_time, w_demand, w_route = weights\n    dx = float(left.x) - float(right.x)\n    dy = float(left.y) - float(right.y)\n    distance = math.hypot(dx, dy)\n    time_gap = abs(float(left.ready_time) - float(right.ready_time)) + abs(float(left.due_time) - float(right.due_time))\n    demand_gap = abs(float(left.demand) - float(right.demand))\n    route_bonus = 0.0 if same_route else 1.0\n    return w_dist * distance + w_time * time_gap + w_demand * demand_gap + w_route * route_bonus\n```\n\nThe same file must also implement worker-side functions:\n\n```python\ndef apply_destroy(solution, context, rng, destroy_id: str, q_ratio: float):\n    \"\"\"Return `(partial_solution, removed_customer_ids, trace)` for D1-D5.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef apply_repair(partial_solution, removed_customer_ids, context, repair_id: str):\n    \"\"\"Return `(candidate_solution, trace)` for R1-R3 using incremental scoring.\"\"\"\n```\n\nImplementation requirements for `apply_destroy`:\n\n- D1 random removal: sample `q` customers without replacement.\n- D2 worst removal: rank customers by `score_reference(full) - score_reference(without_customer)`, descending.\n- D3 Shaw/related removal: choose a seed customer, compute `w1*distance + w2*time-window-gap + w3*demand-gap + w4*same-route-penalty`, remove seed plus most related customers.\n- D4 route removal: remove all customers from the shortest route among the top half by route objective contribution, or all customers from the most expensive route when the top half is empty.\n- D5 segment removal: remove a contiguous segment from one customer-bearing route, with length capped by `q`.\n\nImplementation requirements for `apply_repair`:\n\n- R1 greedy/best insertion: repeatedly choose the globally cheapest feasible insertion.\n- R2 regret-2 insertion: choose the customer with largest `(second_best - best)` before insertion.\n- R3 regret-3 insertion: choose the customer with largest `(third_best - best)`; if only two options exist, use regret-2; if only one exists, use `0`.\n- EV route insertion must call `repair_route_charging`; infeasible insertion candidates must be discarded.\n- Incremental scoring must call `record_repair_delta()` for insertion-option ranking and must not increment `actual_evals`.\n\n- [ ] **Step 2: Add operator tests**\n\nCreate `solver/rl/tests/test_operator_manual.py`:\n\n```python\nfrom dr_alns_ppo.operator_manual import RouletteStats, removal_count, np\nfrom gymnasium import spaces\n\nfrom .action_space import decode_action\nfrom .worker_client import WorkerClient\n\n\nclass SetpAlnsEnv(gym.Env):\n    metadata = {\"render_modes\": []}\n\n    def __init__(self, bundle_dir: str, seed: int = 1, eval_budget: int = 16000, base_temperature: float = 100.0):\n        super().__init__()\n        self.bundle_dir = bundle_dir\n        self.seed_value = int(seed)\n        self.eval_budget = int(eval_budget)\n        self.base_temperature = float(base_temperature)\n        self.action_space = spaces.MultiDiscrete([5, 3, 10, 100])\n        self.observation_space = spaces.Box(low=-10.0, high=10.0, shape=(11,), dtype=np.float32)\n        self.client = WorkerClient(bundle_dir, seed=self.seed_value, max_evals=self.eval_budget)\n        self.last_response = None\n\n    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):\n        super().reset(seed=seed)\n        if seed is not None and int(seed) != self.seed_value:\n            self.client.close()\n            self.seed_value = int(seed)\n            self.client = WorkerClient(self.bundle_dir, seed=self.seed_value, max_evals=self.eval_budget)\n        self.last_response = self.client.reset()\n        return self._obs(self.last_response), {\"actual_evals\": 0}\n\n    def step(self, action):\n        decoded = decode_action(action, base_temperature=self.base_temperature)\n        response = self.client.step(decoded)\n        self.last_response = response\n        reward = self._reward(response)\n        terminated = bool(response[\"actual_evals\"] >= self.eval_budget)\n        truncated = False\n        return self._obs(response), reward, terminated, truncated, response\n\n    def close(self):\n        self.client.close()\n\n    def _reward(self, response):\n        if response.get(\"improved_best\"):\n            return 5.0\n        if response.get(\"improved_current\"):\n            return max(0.01, min(1.0, float(response.get(\"relative_improvement\", 0.0)) * 100.0))\n        return 0.0\n```\n\nObservation vector order:\n\n1. current/best gap;\n2. last-step improvement;\n3. current-is-best flag;\n4. stagnation steps normalized by budget;\n5. budget progress;\n6. current temperature normalized by base temperature;\n7. EV/CV route ratio;\n8. charging action count normalized by route count;\n9. carbon cost share;\n10. quota slack `(quota - E_total) / max(E_total, 1)`;\n11. constraint violation count clipped to 10 and Primary images and media should reveal the actual product, place, object, state, gameplay, or person; you refrain from dark, blurred, cropped, stock-like, or purely atmospheric media when the user needs to inspect the real thing. That is probably fine for `MultiDiscrete`, but stricter validation would catch accidental continuous actions earlier.\\n- [solver/rl/dr_alns_ppo/schemas.py](/Volumes/移动硬盘（512G）/ReSETP/solver/rl/dr_alns_ppo/schemas.py:24): `frozen=True` is shallow. The dict fields use safe `default_factory`, so no shared mutable default bug, but callers can still mutate `metrics`, `solution`, and `trace` contents after construction.\\n- [solver/rl/tests/test_action_space.py](/Volumes/移动硬盘（512G）/ReSETP/solver/rl/tests/test_action_space.py:4): tests cover endpoint happy paths but not invalid dimensions/ranges, raw tuple preservation, or numpy input.\\n\\n### Recommendations\\nAdd small follow-up tests for invalid length, out-of-range components, raw tuple preservation, and `np.array([4, 2, 9, 99])`. Consider widening the annotation with a protocol/`Sequence[int]` or documenting ndarray support. If schemas are meant to be deeply immutable, switch mutable dict fields to immutable mappings at construction time later; otherwise current defaults are safe enough.\\n\\n### Assessment\\nReady to merge? **With fixes** for test coverage/annotation polish, but no correctness blocker in the implemented Task 2 behavior.\"}}"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T18:06:55.876Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_kRAlJhLIqN3atAM0YAAPZaA8","output":"{\"previous_status\":{\"completed\":\"### Strengths\\n\\n- `solution_to_json` is simple and JSON-friendly: `asdict()` produces plain dict/list/scalar structures for the current dataclasses.\\n- Missing top-level keys are handled safely in `solution_from_json` via `payload.get(..., [])`.\\n- The lazy import in `solution_from_json` is appropriate. I verified `dr_alns_ppo.solution_json` imports with only `solver/rl` on `PYTHONPATH`, so PPO-side startup stays import-light.\\n- The focused test passes: `1 passed in 0.02s`.\\n\\n### Issues\\n\\n#### Critical\\n\\nNone.\\n\\n#### Important\\n\\n- [test_solution_json.py](/Volumes/移动硬盘（512G）/ReSETP/solver/rl/tests/test_solution_json.py:5) does not test `cross_site_services`, even though the task requirement explicitly says the bridge must preserve routes, charging actions, and cross-site services. The implementation appears to support it, but the test would not catch a regression in that field.\\n\\n#### Minor\\n\\n- [solution_json.py](/Volumes/移动硬盘（512G）/ReSETP/solver/rl/dr_alns_ppo/solution_json.py:19) reconstructs with `Route(**row)` / `ChargingAction(**row)` / `CrossSiteService(**row)`. That is clean, but less stable for a long-lived JSONL boundary than explicit field mapping. Extra row keys will raise `TypeError`, and scalar/list coercion is not normalized the way the existing `formal_runner._solution_from_dict()` does.\\n- Top-level absent keys are safe, but `null` values are not: `\\\"routes\\\": null` would fail iteration. That is probably acceptable if schemas guarantee arrays, but it is worth keeping in mind for worker error handling.\\n\\n### Recommendations\\n\\n- Add a round-trip test that includes at least one `CrossSiteService`.\\n- Consider explicit reconstruction, matching the style already used in `solver/src/setp_solver/search/formal_runner.py`: cast ids to `str`, numeric fields to `float`, and construct `node_sequence` as a list of strings. This would make the bridge more robust once JSONL worker/client messages become the real boundary.\\n- Keep `solution_from_json` worker-side only unless the PPO runtime intentionally has `solver/src` available.\\n\\n### Assessment\\n\\nReady to merge? **With fixes**\\n\\nThe code itself is likely correct for the current dataclass shape, but the test coverage does not yet prove the full stated Task 3 requirement.\"}}"}}

`removal_count(customer_count, q_ratio)` clips `q_ratio` to 0.10..0.40, returns `ceil(q_ratio * N)`, at least 1 when N>0, 0 when N<=0.\\n- `sa_accept(delta, temperature, random_value)`: better/equal (`delta <= 0`) always accepted; if temperature <= 0 reject worse; otherwise accept iff `random_value < exp(-delta/T)`.\\n- `RouletteStats.record()` reward scores: `global_best=6.0`, `current_improved=3.0`, `accepted_worse=1.0`, unknown/no reward=0.\\n- `RouletteStats.update_segment()`: for each op with uses > 0, `w = lambda*w + (1-lambda)*(score/use)`; reset all scores/uses to zero.\\n- `relatedness()`: `w1*Euclidean distance + w2*(abs(ready diff)+abs(due diff)) + w3*abs(demand diff) + w4*(0 if same_route else 1)`.\\n\\nDestroy operators:\\n- D1 random removal: remove q customers without replacement.\\n- D2 worst removal: rank customers by removal saving, i.e. objective before removal minus objective after removing that customer, descending.\\n- D3 Shaw/related removal: choose seed customer, compute relatedness to all others, remove seed plus most related customers.\\n- D4 route removal: remove all customers from a selected short/expensive customer-bearing route. It is acceptable for D4 to remove route customers even if count differs from q because the operator semantics are whole-route removal.\\n- D5 segment removal: choose one customer-bearing route and remove a contiguous segment capped by q.\\n\\nRepair operators:\\n- R1 greedy/best insertion: repeatedly choose globally cheapest feasible insertion.\\n- R2 regret-2 insertion: choose customer with largest second-best minus best.\\n- R3 regret-3 insertion: choose customer with largest third-best minus best; fall back to regret-2/0 if fewer options.\\n- Insertion scoring must use incremental repair scoring and call `record_repair_delta(context)`; it must not call `score_candidate` during insertion ranking.\\n- EV route insertion must call `repair_route_charging` and discard infeasible EV candidates.\\n- Complete candidate scoring happens later in the worker/env, not inside insertion ranking.\\n\\nTesting requirements in `test_operator_manual.py`:\\n- Include pure tests for `removal_count`, `sa_accept`, `RouletteStats` as in the plan.\\n- Add integration tests using `models/data_bundle/generated_instances/verify_20251113` and existing `setp_solver` utilities to prove:\\n  - D1, D2, D3, and D5 remove at least `ceil(0.1N)` customers on the fixture.\\n  - R2 and R3 produce feasible solutions with `repair_delta_count > 0`.\\n  - EV insertion candidates touching EV routes call `repair_route_charging` indirectly enough to preserve feasibility for EV routes.\\n\\n## Context and Constraints\\n\\nExisting modules available:\\n- `setp_solver.search.evaluation`: `EvaluationContext`, `score_reference`, `record_repair_delta`, maybe `BIG_M`.\\n- `setp_solver.search.charging`: `repair_route_charging`.\\n- `setp_solver.check`: `check_solution`.\\n- `setp_solver.solution`: `Route`, `Solution`.\\n- `setp_solver.search.bundle`: `load_search_bundle`.\\n- `setp_solver.search.construction`: `build_initial_solution`.\\n\\nYou are not alone in the codebase. removed = [cv_customer]\n\n    candidate, _ = apply_repair(partial, removed, context, \"R2\")\n\n    assert calls[\"count\"] > 0\n    assert check_solution(candidate, context.instance, context.prices) <<'PY'\\nfrom pathlib import Path\\nfrom setp_solver.search.bundle import load_search_bundle\\nfrom setp_solver.search.construction import build_initial_solution\\nfrom setp_solver.search.evaluation import EvaluationContext\\nfrom setp_solver.solution import Route, Solution\\nfrom setp_solver.check import check_solution\\nfrom dr_alns_ppo.operator_manual import apply_repair\\n\\nbundle = load_search_bundle(Path('models/data_bundle/generated_instances/verify_20251113'))\\nsolution = build_initial_solution(bundle.instance, bundle.carbon_profile, introduce_ev=True, require_charging_signal=False)\\nprint('routes', len(solution.routes), 'actions', len(solution.charging_actions))\\nfor route in solution.routes:\\n    customers=[n for n in route.node_sequence if n.startswith('C')]\\n    if route.vehicle_type.lower()=='ev':\\n        print(route.vehicle_id, route.node_sequence, customers)\\n\\n# Try removing one customer from EV routes with >=2 customers\\nfor route in solution.routes:\\n    customers=[n for n in route.node_sequence if n.startswith('C')]\\n    if route.vehicle_type.lower()=='ev' and len(customers)>=2:\\n        removed=[customers[0]]\\n        kept=customers[1:]\\n        partial=Solution(routes=[Route(route.vehicle_id, route.vehicle_type, route.home_depot_id, [route.home_depot_id,*kept,route.home_depot_id])])\\n        context=EvaluationContext(bundle.instance,bundle.carbon_profile)\\n        try:\\n            cand, trace=apply_repair(partial, removed, context, 'R2')\\n            print('try', route.vehicle_id, removed, 'trace', trace)\\n            print('viol', check_solution(cand,bundle.instance))\\n        except Exception as e:\\n            print('fail', route.vehicle_id, removed, type(e), e)\\nPY\",\"workdir\":\"/Volumes/移动硬盘（512G）/ReSETP\",\"yield_time_ms\":1000,\"max_output_tokens\":12000}","call_id":"call_5gnWBfpI8fqjhyuoaSFLbVAP"}}

You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. Using your application should feel rich and sophisticated.\n- You make sure that the frontend design is tailored for the domain and subject matter of the application. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.\n- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. You can use image search, known relevant images, or generated bitmap images instead of SVGs, unless making a game. Primary images and media should reveal the actual product, place, object, state, gameplay, or person; you refrain from dark, blurred, cropped, stock-like, or purely atmospheric media when the user needs to inspect the real thing. {"timestamp":"2026-06-15T00:59:55.440Z","type":"compacted","payload":{"message":"","replacement_history":[{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"按 C2 勘察，构建并训练真 Reijnen式 DR-ALNS(PPO控制算子选择)，与现有 solver 依赖隔离，不污染 formal runner。\n[@superpowers](plugin://superpowers@openai-curated-remote)\n制定计划 \n1. 隔离环境: 新建独立 venv/requirements(stable-baselines3==2.4.1, torch==2.5.1, gymnasium==1.0.0, numpy==1.26.4)，放 solver/rl/ 下，与主 solver 仅交换 solution/operator JSON。\n2. SetpAlnsEnv(gymnasium.Env):\n   - state(归一化向量): [current/best gap, 上步改进量, 是否当前最优, 停滞步数, 预算进度, 温度, EV/CV路线比, 充电次数, 碳成本占比, 配额松弛, 约束违反数]\n   - action: MultiDiscrete([5, 3, 10, 100]) = [destroy_id(D1-D5), repair_id(R1-R3占前3), 移除强度档×10, 接受温度档×100]\n   - step: 解码action→用\"强ALNS算子手册\"的D/R算子执行destroy+repair→按所选温度SA接受→更新current/best\n   - reward: 新全局最优+5; 改进当前+小shaped奖励; 否则0\n   - 1次env.step()=1次完整候选评分，对齐16000公平预算\n3. 训练: 在一组SETP训练算例(需生成训练bundle, 勿只用100-01/L-main以防过拟合)上跑PPO; 留held-out验证算例。\n   - 里程碑: 100k步smoke(须打过random-action基线) → 1-2M步pilot → 论文级更多\n4. 推理: PPO.predict(state)→action, 报告 actual_evals 防神经推理导致评估数不足。\n5. 逃生触发: 100k smoke打不过random→不声称DRL改名Reactive; pilot在held-out打不过强化后ALNS→只作future work不入主T3。\n\n产出: SetpAlnsEnv + PPO训练脚本 + smoke(100k)结果(是否>random) + 与强化ALNS的对照。全部在 solver/rl/ 与 solver/reports/dr_alns_ppo/，不动主 solver 与正文。\n"}]},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"【DESTROY 算子集】(轮盘自适应权重选择, 移除量 q 自适应=0.1~0.4×N，关键：禁止固定q=1)\n D1 random removal: 随机移除 q 个客户\n D2 worst removal: 移除\"移除收益\"最高的 q 个(移除后省的成本最大)\n D3 Shaw/related removal: 选种子客户，移除最相关的 q 个；\n     相关度 = w1·距离 + w2·|时间窗差| + w3·|需求差| + w4·(同路线?)\n D4 route removal: 整条(短/贵)路线的客户全移除\n D5 segment removal: 移除某路线一段连续客户\n\n【REPAIR 算子集】(全部增量评分, EV路线触发 repair_route_charging)\n R1 greedy/best insertion: 每个客户插到全局最便宜可行位\n R2 regret-2 insertion: 先插\"(次优-最优)插入成本差\"最大的客户(破解H1的关键，非贪心前瞻)\n R3 regret-3 insertion: regret对前3名\n\n【接受准则】Simulated-Annealing式: 更优必接受; 否则以 exp(-Δ/T) 概率接受;\n T 几何降温 T←αT, α≈0.999, T0 设到\"典型Δ的初始接受率~0.3-0.5\"\n (SA式接受稳健，且正好对接你\"嫁接SA进ALNS\"的后续想法)\n\n【自适应权重】RouletteWheel: 算子得分 +σ1(新全局最优) / +σ2(优于当前) / +σ3(接受但更差);\n 每段更新 w ← λw + (1-λ)(得分/使用次数), λ≈0.8\n"}]},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"我怎么选？\n"}]},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"我同意1\n"}]},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"如果开始跑大型程序了，是那种长时间的等待的，则转为每15分钟探测一次，其余时间静默。如果出结果了，不再长时间运行等待，则恢复活跃。\n"}]},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"提醒：尽可能跑并行，而不是串行，串行太慢了。你继续，我只是提醒。\n"}]},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"怎么还没好？\n\n"}]},{"type":"message","role":"developer","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"<permissions instructions>\nFilesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted.
